items.title: Koosin/Tradition : Femmes et enfants de Bomborokuy invoquent le retour des pluies à travers le « Sãn wele »
items.description: BURKINA-KOOSIN-SOCIETE-TRADITION Koosin/Tradition : Femmes et enfants de Bomborokuy invoquent le retour des pluies à travers le « Sãn wele » Bomborokuy, 16 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Des femmes et des enfants, ont sillonné les rues du village de Bomborokuy ce mercredi 16 septembre 2026, pour implorer le retour des pluies, dans un contexte marqué par des inquiétudes liées à la campagne agricole. Au cours de cette manifestation traditionnelle, les participantes ont parcouru plusieurs artères de la commune en entonnant des chants et en formulant des prières en faveur d’un retour régulier des précipitations. Certaines manifestantes ont, dans un geste symbolique, versé ou jeté de l’eau sur des passants et des connaissances rencontrés sur leur chemin. Cette pratique traditionnelle s'accompagne de démarche et symbolise l’appel à l’eau, avec le souhait de voir les pluies revenir suffisamment sur les champs. Munies de boîtes, de calebasses et de plats, les femmes et les enfants ont ainsi sillonné plusieurs rues du village de Bomborokuy, portant un message d’espoir pour les producteurs dont les cultures dépendent fortement de la régularité des précipitations. Cette mobilisation intervient alors que l’état de certaines cultures dans les champs suscite des inquiétudes. Dans plusieurs parcelles, des plantes présentent des signes de stress hydrique, avec des feuilles qui commencent à se flétrir ou à jaunir, tandis que leur croissance demeure limitée en raison de l’insuffisance des pluies. Pour les producteurs, une reprise régulière des précipitations permettrait aux cultures d’achever leur cycle dans de meilleures conditions et de préserver les espoirs de récolte. Cette mobilisation populaire témoigne de l’importance de la pluie dans la vie quotidienne des populations rurales et de leur attachement aux pratiques traditionnelles, notamment le « Sãn wele », face aux aléas de la saison agricole. Agence d’information du Burkina II/AC/HB/OO

items.title: PM Shehbaz reaches London before heading to New York for UNGA session
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday reached London for a two-day stopover before proceeding to the United States to attend the high-level segment of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. According to a source in the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier would proceed to the US on Saturday to attend the UNGA session. The source said the prime minister was likely to return to the country on Sept 27 or 28 after attending the UNGA session and would again stop over in London for a day or two. “In fact, travelling from Pakistan to the US is quite a long journey, therefore, PM Shehbaz opted to stay somewhere, preferably in London,” the source added. According to the Foreign Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly on Sept 25. “On the sidelines of the UN session, he is expected to hold bilateral meetings with world leaders and participate in high-level events,” the FO said. The prime minister will be accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, federal ministers and senior government officials during the New York leg of the visit. “The premier will present Pakistan’s perspective on regional and global developments and highlight the country’s priorities at the UNGA,” it said. The official theme of the 81st session is ‘Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All’, and the UNGA debate is expected to run from Sept 22 to 26, with a final sitting on Sept 28. However, ongoing fighting between Washington and Tehran is expected to feature prominently in discussions among world leaders, particularly over the security of the Strait of Hormuz, regional stability and the possibility of finding a diplomatic way out of the confrontation. The premier is expected to highlight Pakistan’s efforts to find a peaceful solution to the ongoing US-Iran war.

items.title: Serene Insurance wins three industry awards
items.description: Serene Insurance Ltd has received three awards at two industry events, including two company honours and an individual award for its Head of Underwriting, Mrs Barbara Odoi. The company was named Indigenous Insurance Company of the Year 2025 and Promising Insurance Company of the Year 2025 at the 9th Ghana Insurance Awards held in Accra. The awards ceremony took place on August 22, 2026, at the Labadi Beach Hotel. A week later, Mrs Odoi was named Professional Underwriter of the Year 2025 at the 6th Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana (CIIG) Excellence Awards. Chief Executive Officer of Serene Insurance, Mrs Mercy Naa Koshie Boampong, said the awards reflected the collective efforts of the company’s Board, Management and staff. She said the recognitions reinforced the company’s commitment to strengthening its operations and delivering value to customers and other stakeholders. Congratulating Mrs Odoi, Mrs Boampong said the award highlighted the importance of strong underwriting practices in managing risks and maintaining customer confidence. Mrs Odoi attributed the recognition to teamwork and professional dedication, saying it would motivate her to maintain high standards in underwriting and contribute to improved service delivery. The latest awards add to previous recognition for the company and its leadership. At the 5th CIIG Excellence Awards, Serene Insurance’s Head of Claims, Mr Daniel Otoo, was named Claims Professional of the Year 2024, while Mrs Boampong received the Insurance Professional of the Year 2024 award. Serene Insurance, a member of the First Sky Group, employs more than 97 Ghanaians and has over 280 agents across the country. It serves more than 60,000 institutional and retail clients. The company says its recent growth has been supported by expansion in gross written premiums, underwriting operations, branches and agency networks, as well as efforts to improve claims processing. It says it will continue to focus on innovation, efficient claims settlement and customer-focused products as it expands its presence in Ghana’s insurance market.

items.title: Burkina : Le Président Ibrahim Traoré invite les africains à prouver par le travail et la science qu’ils ne sont pas des « pays de merde »
items.description: Burkina : Le Président Ibrahim Traoré invite les africains à prouver par le travail et la science qu’ils ne sont pas des « pays de merde » Bobo-Dioulasso, 17 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré a invité le vendredi 11 septembre 2026, à Bobo-Dioulasso, les africains à prouver au monde par le travail et la science qu’ils ne sont pas des « pays de merde ». Dans sa déclaration à l’Université Nazi Boni de Bobo-Dioulasso, le vendredi 11 septembre 2026, le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré a rappelé les propos du Président américain Donald Trump qui qualifiait il y a quelques années, les États africains de « pays de merde ». « En son temps, cela m'a beaucoup fait mal », a confié le Président Traoré « mais en analysant la situation », il estime que Trump « n'a peut-être pas tort ». Pour le Capitaine Traoré, les propos de Trump peuvent se justifier par l’attitude même des africains qui ont pris l’habitude lorsque leurs femmes enceintes sont presque à terme, d’aller fait naître leurs enfants aux États-Unis pour avoir la nationalité américaine pour ces enfants. Cette conduite qui n’honore pas les africains a été interdite par le Président américain et le Chef de l’État Ibrahim Traoré s’en réjouit. « Donald Trump a mis fin à ça, moi je le félicite pour ça. C’est très bien. C'est l'un des actes que j'ai appréciés parce qu'il faut qu'on arrête nous-mêmes de nous auto-flageller, de nous insulter nous-mêmes », a-t-il affirmé. Pour le Camarade Président Ibrahim Traoré, les enfants africains doivent naitre sur le continent, prendre la nationalité de leurs pays et se battre pour transformer leurs patries au lieu d’aller quémander la nationalité des personnes qui se sont battues pour construire leurs nations. Il a estimé que les propos de Trump font mal mais doivent motiver les africains à se battre par le travail et la science afin de transformer leurs pays comme le Burkina Faso est en train de le faire. Le Burkina Faso pleinement engagé dans la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) depuis le 30 septembre 2022, travaille à son industrialisation et son développement avec ses propres moyens. A cet effet, le Chef de l’État a procédé aux inaugurations du Complexe industriel Textile des Forces armées du Burkina (TEXFORCES-BF) le mercredi 9 septembre 2026 et du complexe d'amphithéâtres construit dans le cadre de l'Initiative présidentielle pour une Éducation de Qualité pour tous (IPEQ), le vendredi 11 septembre 2026. Ils ont été financés par des fonds burkinabè. Le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré a renouvelé son invitation aux étudiants burkinabè à embrasser les filières scientifiques. Même ceux qui ont fait des filières littéraires, il leur a conseillé de se reformer dans les filières techniques. Il reconnait qu’on a besoin des littéraires pour faire « passer des messages, conscientiser, faire reculer l'ignorance » mais précise qu’« on n’en a pas besoin beaucoup » car « l’avenir, c'est dans la technique », a-t-il répété. Le Président Ibrahim Traoré a relevé qu’un investisseur nigérian a été contraint de recruter de la main d’œuvre à l’extérieur de son pays pour sa raffinerie qu’il a mis en place parce qu’il n’y avait pas de ressources humaines qualifiées sur place. Pour le fonctionnement de TEXFORCES-BF et des Industries à venir, le Chef de l’État veut des Burkinabè. « Il faut former la jeunesse à maintenir ces machines, à les faire fonctionner, à les entretenir et à reproduire ces machines », a-t-il insisté. Il a exprimé sa joie de constater que des étudiants ont participé aux travaux de construction du complexe de l’amphithéâtres et que son équipement ait été assuré par des artisans burkinabè. Ce qui a permis de maintenir au pays au profit des Burkinabè, les milliards qui ont servi aux travaux de construction et d’équipements. « C'est ça la révolution économique également. Et nous sommes en mesure de le faire », a-t-il affirmé. Le Chef de l’État prévoit la construction d’ici la fin de l’année « d'une industrie de tannerie » par l’expertise burkinabè. Il a annoncé que le Burkina Faso ne va plus importer de matières pour fabriquer le ciment parce que nous avons tout le matériel sur place et nous avons le cerveau nécessaire pour les transformer ici et pour participer à la construction de notre pays. « Je crois en la jeunesse, je crois en vos capacités. Croyez en vous et apprenez », a-t-il souligné. Agence d’Information du Burkina CS/AB/wis

items.title: PM’s fuel subsidy scheme faces first-day hurdles at petrol pumps
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The much-touted fuel subsidy scheme launched by the prime minister faced snags on Thursday, the first day of its nationwide rollout, as many petrol pumps declined to honour the digital app, claiming they lacked the system needed to provide petrol at Rs100 per litre less. After receiving several complaints in this regard, Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima visited various fuel stations in Rawalpindi to ensure that subsidised petrol was available to registered consumers. A day earlier, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) expressed concerns that its members were unaware of the subsidy disbursement mechanism and feared they would have to run from pillar to post to recover the amount. However, to resolve the matter, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, along with officials from the relevant ministries, held a meeting with the PPDA on Thursday to discuss the mechanism for implementing the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme. PPDA Chairman Malik Khuda Baksh led the delegation, which joined the meeting via video link. The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) briefed the participants on the reimbursement mechanism and assured them that claims submitted under the scheme would be processed within 48 hours, ensuring timely payments to participating petroleum dealers. The Ministry of IT and Telecommunications briefed the participants on the digital system developed to implement the scheme. The meeting was also informed that a dedicated control room had been established to assist petrol pumps and address their queries and complaints. Petrol pumps can contact the control room at 9772 for assistance. The meeting was further informed that funds for three months had been earmarked for the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme, with Rs25 billion for the first month already provided to SBP to facilitate timely reimbursement under the scheme. The PPDA chairman said the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme was welcomed by petroleum dealers, but a lack of information about the disbursement of subsidy amounts was creating confusion among its members. “We assure you that all our members across the country will support the PM’s fuel relief scheme,” Khuda Baksh said. During the meeting, the petroleum minister appreciated the cooperation extended by petroleum dealers and emphasised the importance of close coordination among all stakeholders for the effective, transparent and timely implementation of the relief initiative. OCAC warns of disruption In another development, the Oil Companies Advisory Committee (OCAC) warned the government of disruption to the oil supply chain if Rs67 billion in price differential claims (PDC) pending since March 2026 were not settled. In a letter to the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) chairman, the OCAC claimed that the pending PDC amount was equivalent to five imported cargoes of petrol. The letter, written by OCAC Secretary General Dr Nazir Abbas Zaidi, was forwarded to the petroleum minister and the Petroleum Division secretary. It said oil companies were now unable to finance an uninterrupted fuel supply chain due to Rs66.7 billion in outstanding PDCs. The OCAC said the situation had been further aggravated by the evolving geopolitical environment and potential disruptions to regional supply routes, including the East-West Pipeline. The oil companies warned that the country could face significant supply-side challenges under the current regional scenario, while the oil industry’s liquidity continued to deplete due to a lack of support from the authorities. “Any resulting supply-chain disruption must not be on account of the oil industry,” the OCAC said in the letter. Despite repeated communications and extensive verification and audit processes, the OCAC had requested settlement by June 8, 2026, but the matter remained unresolved, it added. “We urge Ogra to urgently conclude the verification process and release all verified and approved claims, including the approved premium differential claims relating to Motor Spirit (petrol) imports during the recent geopolitical crisis, referring to the situation arising following the US-Israeli attack on Iran at the end of February 2026.” The OCAC said oil marketing companies (OMCs) had consistently supported the government, particularly when fuel security and uninterrupted supplies were at stake. “Yet today, the same industry is facing an acute and worsening liquidity crisis and effectively being required to finance the supply chain while its own liquidity is being progressively drained,” the OCAC said, inviting government functionaries to meet its members at its head office in Karachi. The OCAC also reminded the government of the need to revise OMC margins, adding that they were last revised in September 2023 and had remained unchanged despite significant increases in operating, financing, technology, regulatory and compliance costs. The letter added that dealer margins were increased by Rs1.34 per litre in August 2026, while the approved Rs1.22 per litre increase in OMC margins remained to be notified and implemented. “Unlike dealers, OMCs carry the full responsibility for product procurement, import financing, inventory management, logistics and ensuring product availability across the country, in addition to meeting ever-expanding regulatory and digitisation requirements, with implementation timelines being progressively compressed,” the letter said. It demanded immediate notification and implementation of the Rs1.22 per litre increase in OMC margins and the establishment of a predictable mechanism for periodic margin revisions.

items.title: Dr Charity Binka charges media to inform, monitor and shape Affirmative Action implementation
items.description: Chair of the African Women Leaders Network (AWLN), Dr Charity Binka, has urged the media to play three key roles in ensuring the effective implementation of Ghana’s Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024 (Act 1121). She identified the roles as informing the public, monitoring implementation and influencing the narrative around women’s participation in leadership. Speaking at a capacity-building workshop for women in media organised by the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Binka said the passage of the law was an important milestone, but its success would depend largely on how it was implemented. “Passing a law is different from living it. Implementation is where many laws fail and where the media must not fail,” she said. Dr Binka said the media had a responsibility to ensure that the law did not remain confined to legal documents but was understood by people across the country. Dr Binka said women in the media had three key roles to play in ensuring the Act translated into practical change: informing the public, monitoring implementation and influencing the narrative around women in leadership. She urged journalists to simplify the law and take its provisions beyond legal and official documents to platforms where ordinary citizens could understand them. “We have to take the Act from our legal books into our languages, our morning shows, our community radio, our community information centres,” she said. “We’ve got to make it simple and be able for people to understand it.” She said the media also had a responsibility to monitor institutions and establish which organisations were complying with the law. “Our stories, our investigations, and follow-ups will keep institutions accountable,” she said. Dr Binka further urged media organisations to challenge stereotypes and give women greater opportunities to contribute to public discussions as experts and leaders. “You must promote women as leaders, as experts, and as capable. We have to stop the stereotyping,” she said. She cited media coverage of economic issues as an example, saying women were sometimes overlooked as commentators on subjects such as national budgets. “When they do the budgets, they don’t look for women to talk about the budgets. They look for men because they think they are the economy,” she said. Dr Binka said journalists could only effectively monitor the implementation of the law if they understood its provisions, the obligations it placed on public and private institutions and the mechanisms available for monitoring compliance. “We cannot do all this without understanding the law and becoming champions of implementation,” she said. She said a proper understanding of the Act would give journalists the confidence to engage institutions and demand accountability. Dr Binka also stressed that affirmative action was not about replacing merit with gender. “Let us remember that affirmative action is not about replacing merit with gender,” she said. “It is about addressing structural barriers that historically prevented qualified women from having equal opportunities to participate in elections.” She called for women to work across sectors, share knowledge, mentor one another, and collectively demand accountability as implementation of the law progresses. “The law has opened the door. But it is our collective action that will keep it open for generations of women in the years to come,” she said. Dr Binka said the passage of Act 1121 had created an important opportunity, but the responsibility now rested with stakeholders to ensure that women and girls across Ghana could take advantage of it. “Our responsibility now is to ensure that the door remains open. And that women and girls across Ghana are able to walk through it. Participate, lead, and contribute fully to national development,” she said. The Affirmative Action Act 2024 is expected to ensure that a critical number of women hold key positions in governance, public life, and decision-making spaces, thereby improving the lives of women in the country.

items.title: UFOA-A U17 : le Sénégal étrille la Guinée (3-0) et file en finale
items.description: Les Lionceaux n'ont laissé planer aucun doute. Ce jeudi au stade Léopold Sédar Senghor, le Sénégal s'est imposé 3-0 face à la Guinée en demi-finale de l'UFOA-A U17 2026, validant du même coup sa qualification pour la finale et pour la prochaine Coupe d'Afrique des nations de la catégorie. La physionomie du match a rapidement tourné à l'avantage des joueurs de Lamine Sané. Après une occasion guinéenne sans conséquence dès la 5e minute, les Sénégalais ont pris les commandes à la 13e : sur un coup franc parfaitement botté par Maguette Gueye, Moussa Ndiaye a devancé tout le monde de la tête pour ouvrir le score. Un but qui faisait presque écho aux mots prononcés la veille par le sélectionneur en conférence de presse, insistant sur la profondeur de son effectif. La Guinée a tenté de réagir, sans jamais parvenir à inquiéter réellement le gardien et capitaine Assane Sarr. En seconde période, le Sénégal a fait le break à la 85e minute par Souleymane Commissaire Faye, avant que Cheikh Thior n'ajoute un troisième but dans le temps additionnel, scellant définitivement la victoire des Lionceaux. Avec ce succès, le Sénégal confirme un parcours quasiment parfait dans ce tournoi qu'il organise à domicile : deux larges victoires en phase de groupes face à la Mauritanie (4-0) et la Sierra Leone (5-0), un nul vierge contre la Gambie, puis cette démonstration en demi-finale, sans avoir encaissé le moindre but jusqu'ici. Les Lionceaux valident également leur billet pour la prochaine CAN U17, et abordent cette échéance avec le statut de champions d'Afrique en titre, après leur sacre continental décroché plus tôt cette année au Maroc. Une double ambition anime donc désormais le groupe de Lamine Sané : conserver la couronne africaine et confirmer sa suprématie régionale. Car le Sénégal n'est pas un simple prétendant dans cette zone UFOA-A : les Lionceaux sont les tenants du titre du tournoi, vainqueurs de l'édition 2025 disputée à Bamako, après avoir déjà triomphé en 2024 sur leurs propres terres. Les Sénégalais connaîtront leur adversaire en finale à l'issue de l'autre demi-finale, qui oppose la Gambie au Liberia ce jeudi à 19h00, toujours au stade Léopold Sédar Senghor. Les deux finalistes de ce choc décrocheront eux aussi leur ticket pour la CAN U17. Rendez-vous est donné le dimanche 20 septembre pour la finale, ainsi que pour la petite finale, qui clôtureront ce tournoi qualificatif organisé au Sénégal depuis le 7 septembre. C.G. DIOP

items.title: Afarinick, Meiji deepen partnership to advance sustainable cocoa production
items.description: Ghanaian-owned farm and agroforestry restoration company, Afarinick Company Limited (ACL), has partnered with Japan’s Meiji Co. Ltd. to develop a sustainable and circular agroforestry cocoa model in Ghana. The two companies signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) in Accra on Monday, September 14, 2026, as part of activities marking 100 years of Meiji Milk Chocolate and the Japanese company’s longstanding relationship with Ghana. The agreement was signed by Afarinick Executive Chairman Joe Forson and Meiji President and Representative Director Bunjiro Yao. It provides a framework for the joint development of an agroforestry cocoa farm, with the productive use of farm waste as a key component. The proposed model will combine cocoa production with agroforestry and the reuse of materials generated within the farming system to improve resource efficiency and promote more sustainable cocoa production. The signing ceremony was attended by representatives of the Government of Ghana, the Ghana Cocoa Board, the Embassy of Japan and other stakeholders. Afarinick operates in farm management, forest restoration, sustainable agriculture, reforestation and geographic information systems (GIS), among other areas. The company also owns what it describes as Ghana’s largest privately owned sustainable cocoa plantation — a 2,000-acre commercial farm in the Volta Region. The plantation combines cocoa with plantain and indigenous trees and uses irrigation and other climate-smart land-management practices. The partnership with Meiji will expand Afarinick’s work in Ghana’s cocoa value chain, particularly efforts to create additional value from waste and other resources generated on cocoa farms. The companies are expected to use the proposed farm as a model for integrating cocoa production, agroforestry and circular resource use. For Ghana’s cocoa sector, the partnership could provide a framework for exploring how farm waste can be utilised while improving the environmental sustainability of cocoa production.

items.title: FTH Owerri: We didn’t shut down, disruption due to system upgrade
items.description: By Emmanuel Iheaka OWERRI — The management of the Federal Teaching Hospital Owerri has said the disruption of some of its services in the last 48 hours was caused by a scheduled upgrade of its Electronic Medical Record (EMR) system. The hospital, in a statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Ikechukwu Anyaegbu, said the upgrade to a newer and more advanced version was part of its efforts to improve the efficiency, accessibility, security and overall quality of healthcare services. Anyaegbu dismissed reports circulating on social media that the hospital deliberately shut down its system to deny patients and members of the public access to healthcare. He also refuted claims that 10 people died as a result of the system upgrade, describing the attribution of deaths to the exercise as a misrepresentation of the complex medical and life-threatening emergencies managed at the hospital. “There was no shutdown of clinical services. The hospital’s wards were onboarded to the new system ahead of the system going live, as part of the planned transition. “Clinics also remained operational, and alternative processes were deployed to support continuity of care during the transition,” the statement said. According to the hospital, the upgrade was also intended to strengthen its digital health infrastructure, facilitate telemedicine services, improve patient data management and align its systems with evolving global practices. Management, however, acknowledged that technical difficulties and workflow challenges associated with the migration had caused inconvenience, anxiety and delays in some services. “The hospital’s Management, ICT unit, clinical teams, and relevant technical consultants have remained actively engaged throughout the transition. They are working round the clock to identify and resolve emerging technical issues and to stabilise the new system,” the statement added. The hospital said significant progress had been recorded within the last 24 hours, with full service restored in many units. It added that the outstanding technical challenges were expected to be substantially resolved within the next 48 hours. The management apologised to patients, staff and members of the public for the disruptions and appealed for patience and understanding. It reaffirmed its commitment to providing safe, accessible and quality healthcare services to residents of Imo State and beyond. The hospital also said it would continue to invest in technology and processes to improve patient care while strengthening contingency measures to minimise disruptions during major software upgrades and system migrations. The post FTH Owerri: We didn’t shut down, disruption due to system upgrade appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana launches food warning label campaign as NCDs account for nearly 45% of deaths
items.description: The Ministry of Health, in partnership with SEND Ghana and other stakeholders, has launched a mass media campaign to promote front-of-package warning labels and help Ghanaians make more informed food choices. The campaign comes against the backdrop of a growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs), including hypertension, diabetes, cancer and cardiovascular diseases, which account for nearly 45% of deaths in Ghana. It seeks to raise public awareness of the health risks associated with excessive consumption of foods high in sugar, salt and unhealthy fats. Through the campaign, consumers will be educated on how to identify front-of-package warning labels and use the information to make healthier choices when buying food products. Health experts are also concerned about the increasing exposure of children and young people to unhealthy diets, with calls for prevention efforts to begin early. Director of Technical Coordination at the Ministry of Health, Dr Hafez Adam Taher, said public education on unhealthy eating must extend beyond adults to include children. “We’ve been concentrating on the adults, and we’re saying let’s focus on the children. When we introduce children from the early stages to sugary foods, it gets difficult for them to stop as they grow. Let’s extend the scope on unhealthy eating to include our children.” Dr Taher also urged Ghanaians to pay greater attention to what they eat and called on food manufacturers to provide clear information about the nutritional content of their products. Country Director of SEND Ghana, Harriet Nuema Agyemang, said access to clear and understandable information was essential to helping consumers make healthier choices. “We can prevent non-communicable diseases if we have clear information to help us make the choices we need to make.” She urged the public to support efforts by the Ministry of Health to promote healthier eating habits and reduce the risk of diet-related diseases. The campaign forms part of broader efforts to address the burden of NCDs in Ghana through public education, prevention and the promotion of healthier lifestyles.

items.title: Punjab Assembly begins evaluation of AI use in public services
items.description: LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly has begun parliamentary evaluation of artificial intelligence and digital governance, with its Special Committee No. 13 examining the use of AI in public services and the safeguards needed to protect citizens’ rights. Chaired by Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan, the committee held its inaugural meeting on Thursday. It is the first parliamentary committee in Pakistan and the South Asian region with a dedicated mandate covering artificial intelligence and digital governance. The meeting followed a three-day workshop for committee members, held in Islamabad from Sept 2 to 4 by UNDP Pakistan and the United Kingdom’s international development organisation. The workshop examined artificial intelligence and digital technologies, their potential benefits and risks, and the principles of responsible governance. The committee considered an initial programme of parliamentary inquiry into the use of AI in Punjab, focusing on transparency, accountability, citizens’ rights, data security, effective remedies and meaningful human oversight. Two provincial public service systems were identified for initial examination. The first is the Punjab Safe Cities Authority’s AI-assisted e-challan system . The committee will examine the accuracy of violation detection, human validation of violations, citizens’ access to evidence, mechanisms for challenging and reviewing decisions, and the handling of related data. The second relates to welfare assistance linked to the Punjab Socio-Economic Registry (PSER). The committee will examine registration and accessibility, data accuracy, eligibility assessments, explanations for adverse decisions, correction of inaccurate information and opportunities for reconsideration. Importantly, the committee said it would establish through evidence how eligibility was actually determined — whether through manual assessment, fixed rules, statistical scoring, machine learning or a combination of these methods — rather than assuming that AI was involved. The committee also discussed the constitutional and legal implications of emerging digital technologies, including digital harms, deepfakes, threats to democratic trust, risks to women and vulnerable groups, data governance and institutional capacity.

items.title: Lachgar salue la gestion marocaine du dossier de Sebta et recentre le débat sur le Sahara
items.description: Alors que la question migratoire entre le Maroc et l’Espagne continue d’alimenter les débats politiques et médiatiques de l’autre côté de la Méditerranée, Driss Lachgar, premier secrétaire de l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP), a estimé que les événements liés à Sebta et Melilla ne doivent pas détourner l’attention des priorités nationales du Royaume. Invité de l'émission « La voie vers les élections 2026 », Driss Lachgar a été interpellé sur le vote, ce jeudi, du Parlement européen appelant le Maroc et l’Espagne à renvoyer les migrants ayant franchi les frontières de la ville occupée de Sebta. Dans sa réponse, le dirigeant socialiste a tenu à distinguer « la présence d’un événement dans l’actualité » de « la question de Sebta et Melilla » en tant que dossier politique. Selon lui, l’USFP a adopté une position claire lors de la crise migratoire. « Nous n’avons pas voulu attribuer la responsabilité au gouvernement marocain », a-t-il affirmé, soulignant qu’une telle attitude aurait pu être exploitée par « l’extrême droite » et « tous ceux qui s’opposent aux migrants », avec des répercussions potentielles sur la communauté marocaine établie à l’étranger. Driss Lachgar a dénoncé certaines perceptions européennes à l’égard des migrants, rappelant que des dirigeants issus de la droite européenne considéraient les marocains comme des « zombies » contre lesquelles il fallait ériger des barrières pour protéger l’Europe. À l’inverse, il a salué « la gestion sage » de la situation par le Maroc, sous la conduite du Roi Mohammed VI, ainsi que les orientations adoptées afin d’éviter toute escalade des tensions. © Mounir Mehimdate Le premier secrétaire de l’USFP a également mis en avant l’attitude du gouvernement socialiste espagnol de Pedro Sanchez qui, selon lui, a résisté aux pressions exercées par la droite et l’extrême droite pour détériorer les relations avec Rabat et lui imputer la responsabilité de la vague migratoire observée à l’époque. Pour Driss Lachgar, toute tentative d’escalade risquerait avant tout de détourner l’attention des priorités stratégiques du pays. « Nous avons mis en garde contre toute escalade », a-t-il déclaré, estimant qu’elle ne ferait que modifier l’agenda des priorités nationales. Le responsable politique a ainsi replacé au centre des préoccupations la question du Sahara marocain. À l’approche de la réunion du Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies prévue en octobre, il a souligné que la cause nationale demeure au cœur des orientations souveraines du Royaume et de sa politique extérieure. © Mounir Mehimdate « Nous considérons que Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI a largement réussi dans la gestion de ces dossiers », a-t-il affirmé, estimant que la priorité devait désormais être accordée à « la mise en œuvre des mécanismes découlant de la résolution 2703 du Conseil de sécurité », afin d’« entrer dans une phase d’application de l’initiative d’autonomie ». Interrogé enfin sur l’annonce évoquant une élévation du niveau de représentation diplomatique entre le Maroc et Israël à l’ouverture d’ambassades, alors qu’aucune communication officielle n’a été faite par les autorités marocaines, Driss Lachgar s’est montré prudent. © Mounir Mehimdate « Sur les questions souveraines et les grands dossiers nationaux, je ne peux pas me permettre de fonder mon appréciation sur des sources extérieures », a-t-il déclaré. Avant toute évaluation, il dit attendre une position officielle du gouvernement marocain. « T ant que je n’aurai pas entendu une position officielle de notre gouvernement, et tant qu’aucune annonce n’aura été faite par les autorités marocaines, il m’est difficile de porter un quelconque jugement sur cet événement et sur ses éventuelles implications », a conclu le dirigeant de l’USFP. The post Lachgar salue la gestion marocaine du dossier de Sebta et recentre le débat sur le Sahara appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Pakistan, China reaffirm consensus at inaugural Boundary Joint Commission meeting
items.description: The inaugural meeting of the Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission (BJC) concluded in Islamabad on Thursday, with both sides reaffirming their consensus and agreeing on a framework for future cooperation under the commission. According to the Foreign Office (FO), the meeting was held in Islamabad on Sept 16 and 17, marking the formal launch of the commission. The BJC was envisaged under the 2013 China-Pakistan Agreement on the Boundary Management System. “Both sides described the establishment of the commission as a vital milestone in further strengthening the Pakistan-China All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership,” the FO said. According to the statement, discussions at the inaugural meeting covered a wide range of matters related to border management and cooperation, including cross-border coordination, the movement of goods and people, joint border surveys and people-to-people linkages. The meeting concluded with the signing of the minutes, reaffirming the two sides’ consensus and setting out a framework for future cooperation under the commission, the statement said. “Both sides agreed to hold the next meeting of the commission in China on mutually convenient dates,” the FO said. The Pakistan delegation was led by Bilal Mahmood Chaudhary, Director General (China) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while the Chinese delegation was led by Li Ya, Deputy Director General of the Department of Boundary and Ocean Affairs at China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Other representatives from the ministries of foreign affairs, defence, interior, commerce and communications, as well as customs, survey and other boundary management authorities, also attended the meeting. The commission has its origins in the 2013 Agreement on the Boundary Management System , signed during the visit of then Chinese Premier Li Keqiang to Islamabad. Article 45 of the agreement provides for the establishment of the joint commission to oversee the implementation of border management arrangements. The mechanism will provide an institutional framework for dealing with practical issues along the border, including the maintenance and inspection of the boundary, joint surveys, boundary marker issues, the management of cross-border facilities and the handling of incidents involving the border. Its activation also gives the two countries a mechanism for regular coordination on a border that is important for movement between Pakistan and China, including thr­ough the Khunjerab crossing, and for trade and connectivity linked to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

items.title: EU Kids Act : l’Europe veut durcir l’accès des mineurs aux réseaux sociaux
items.description: L’Union européenne a présenté jeudi les grandes lignes de son projet de loi destiné à mieux protéger les mineurs en ligne. Le texte prévoit une interdiction des réseaux sociaux avant 13 ans, des comptes fortement encadrés entre 13 et 15 ans et la suppression de plusieurs fonctionnalités jugées addictives pour les moins de 18 ans. L’Union européenne veut renforcer la protection des enfants et des adolescents sur les plateformes numériques. Présenté par la Commission européenne, le projet baptisé « Kids Act » prévoit une approche progressive en fonction de l’âge. Les moins de 13 ans ne pourraient plus accéder aux réseaux sociaux concernés par le dispositif. Entre 13 et 14 ans, les jeunes pourraient disposer de « mini-comptes » créés et contrôlés par leurs parents. Leur utilisation serait limitée à une heure par jour, tandis que les contacts devraient être préalablement approuvés par les parents. À partir de 15 ans, les adolescents pourraient créer leurs propres comptes sans intervention parentale. Fin du défilement illimité Le projet prévoit également de limiter les fonctionnalités considérées comme susceptibles d'encourager une utilisation excessive des plateformes. Pour les moins de 18 ans, le défilement illimité, les notifications destinées à pousser à la connexion ou encore certains systèmes de récompenses et de pénalités seraient notamment concernés. Des pauses obligatoires et des limites de temps pourraient également être instaurées afin de préserver le sommeil et les activités scolaires. Ces règles concerneraient non seulement les réseaux sociaux, mais aussi certaines plateformes de partage vidéo, services de jeux vidéo et applications intégrant des fonctionnalités jugées à risque. La Commission souhaite par ailleurs encadrer les assistants et chatbots d’intelligence artificielle. Selon Henna Virkkunen, ils ne devraient notamment plus pouvoir se présenter comme des « amis humains » afin d’exercer une influence émotionnelle sur les enfants. Une vérification de l’âge obligatoire Pour faire respecter ces restrictions, les plateformes devront vérifier l’âge de leurs utilisateurs lors de la création des comptes. Bruxelles prévoit de mettre à disposition une solution destinée à permettre cette vérification tout en préservant l’anonymat des utilisateurs. Les plateformes pourront également utiliser d’autres technologies publiques offrant des garanties équivalentes. En cas de non-respect des règles, les opérateurs pourraient être exposés à des amendes pouvant atteindre 6 % de leur chiffre d’affaires annuel mondial, conformément au niveau maximal déjà prévu par le Digital Services Act (DSA). La Commission européenne entend également aller plus loin. Un autre texte, le Digital Fairness Act, doit être présenté à l’automne afin d’envisager un encadrement plus large des fonctionnalités jugées addictives, y compris pour les utilisateurs adultes. items.title: Imaan Mazari, husband sent on judicial remand in another case after SC suspends sentences
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Hours after the Supreme Court suspended the sentences of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) rejected police’s request for a 30-day physical remand of the couple and sent them to jail on judicial remand. On January 24, an Islamabad sessions court sentenced Imaan and Hadi to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). The convictions of the couple, who had already been jailed the day before in a separate case, were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts . Islamabad ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain passed the order after the two accused were produced before the court for a hearing in a case registered against them at Kohsar police station. Soon after their release, Islamabad police personnel, led by the SSP Operations, reached Adiala jail and arrested the two again in connection with the case registered at Kohsar police station. The police subsequently produced them before the ATC late at night. Former federal minister Shireen Mazari confirmed the development, saying attempts were being made to keep the couple in jail. Speaking to Dawn , Imaan’s counsel Riasat Ali Azad also confirmed the development, saying a large contingent of Islamabad police had shifted the couple to Kohsar police station. The case at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station was registered on March 22, 2025, on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio. Imaan and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added. The FIR included Section 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), Section 341 (wrongful restraint), Section 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), Section 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and Section 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties). SC suspends sentences Earlier today, the apex court suspended their sentences after a two-judge SC bench, headed by Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, took up the couple’s appeals against the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) refusal in February to suspend the sentences. On Thursday, the SC granted the couple bail against surety bonds of Rs200,000 and ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict. “Both are lawyers and we are keeping their honour,” observed Justice Afghan, but also asked senior counsel Faisal Siddiqui, the couple’s lawyer, to tell the appellants to observe the court’s decorum. “There is a difference between a lawyer and an ordinary person,” the judge observed. According to a written order, the SC converted the petitions of both Imaan and Hadi into appeals and suspended the operation of the January 24 conviction. The court also ordered the release of petitioners — noting they were practising advocates — on bail till the decision of their pending appeals before IHC. The release was subject to furnishing personal surety bonds worth Rs200,000 for each with the SC’s additional registrar (judicial). The SC will issue a detailed verdict on the case later. Earlier, the SC had repeatedly adjourned hearings in the case on the grounds that the IHC had fixed their application for suspension of sentence along with the main appeal. During Thursday’s hearing, Siddiqui argued that the SC had issued its first order on May 12 in which the IHC was asked to decide the applicants’ petition for suspension of sentence as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of two weeks. On May 12, the SC ordered the IHC to decide Imaan and Hadi’s sentence suspension pleas within two weeks. Despite the May 26 deadline having already passed, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) challenged the SC order and sought its withdrawal. During the proceedings, Siddiqui also read out the order sheets from various IHC hearings. At one point, the SC directed Additional Attorney General (AAG) Rana Asadullah Khan, who was standing at the rostrum, to take a seat, adding that the court will hear Siddiqui first. “Let him sit, though he has certainly worn us out,” Siddiqui quipped and cited former chief justice Asif Saeed Khosa’s remarks that a case would only be adjourned upon the death of a judge or a lawyer. The counsel regretted that the IHC adjourned the case multiple times and that his clients’ request for an early hearing was rejected by the high court’s registrar office. “What transpired at the high court came as a surprise to us,” the counsel said. “These days are an era of surprises,” remarked Justice Ibrahim. During the hearing, the AAG contended that the IHC has not yet issued any adverse ruling, adding that seven opportunities were provided in the trial court. He highlighted that the judicial forum for the suspension of a sentence under Section 426 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) was the high court. Justice Afghan observed that the IHC always cited the SC directives for early disposal of the case but does not act upon them. The judge also asked AAG Khan whether he would give any assurance that proceedings would be held at the next IHC hearing, to which the latter replied that he cannot represent any high court judge in the SC. Later, the SC suspended the sentence of the applicants and ordered their release on bail, pending the IHC’s final verdict. In their applications, the applicants had stated that it was a settled policy of the SC that criminal matters have to be given priority, especially when the matters pertain to bail or suspension of sentence. Moreover, in Section 7 of the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023, it was expressly stated that any application pleading urgency shall be fixed for hearing within a period of 14 days. The application contended that Imaan was a young female lawyer and has remained incarcerated for a long period of time in a case where conviction was the “result of a sham trial”. The case Imaan and Hadi have been in jail since their arrest on January 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association (IHCBA) president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial. Just a day later, a sessions court convicted Imaan and Hadi in the social media posts case. It sentenced the duo to 10 years’ imprisonment under Section 10 (cyber terrorism), five years’ imprisonment under Section 9 (glorification of an offence) and two years’ imprisonment under Section 26-A (false and fake information) of Peca. All sentences were to run concurrently. The case stemmed from a complaint filed on Aug 12, 2025 by the assistant director (investigating officer) at the NCCIA Islamabad, before the Federal Investigation Agency’s Cybercrime Reporting Centre. The complaint accused Imaan of disseminating and “propagating narratives that align with hostile terrorist groups and proscribed organisations”, while her husband was implicated for reposting some of her posts. The first information report (FIR) in the case alleged that the two held security forces responsible for cases of missing persons in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. It also stated that they had portrayed the armed forces as ineffective against proscribed groups, including the banned outfits Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) and the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). Judge Majoka had indicted Imaan and Hadi in the case on Oct 30, 2025 and issued arrest warrants for the couple on Nov 5, 2025. The judge then reissued arrest warrants for them in January after repeated non-appearances. After being convicted, the couple challenged the sentences by filing separate appeals in the IHC on February 7. Taking up those appeals and sentence suspension pleas on February 19, the IHC issued notices to the respondents but refused to suspend the sentences. On April 30, Imaan and Hadi moved a separate appeal before the SC against the IHC’s February order. They sought an early hearing of the plea in June, after which notices were issued on July 6. After the SC’s intervention , the IHC finally declared the jailed couple’s pleas seeking suspension of sentences as admissible on July 25. Days later, Imaan moved the SC again seeking an early hearing of the challenge against the IHC order. Additional input by Mohammad Asghar

items.title: Ashanti region records 25% drop in maternal mortality in first half of 2026
items.description: The Ashanti Region has recorded a 25% drop in institutional maternal mortality in the first half of 2026, with the rate falling from 199.5 to 148.7 deaths per 100,000 live births. The Ashanti Regional Health Directorate attributed the improvement to targeted clinical interventions and the expansion of care at peripheral health facilities. Regional Director of Health Services, Dr Fred Adomako-Boateng, announced the figures during the region’s 2026 mid-year health performance review. “The maternal mortality ratio for the last half 2024 mid-year was 158 maternal deaths per 100,000. In 2025, it was 199.5 maternal deaths per 100,000. Ladies and gentlemen, for 2026, it’s 148.7 per 100,000. Ladies and gentlemen, it means for the region Ashanti region, we have reduced maternal mortality by 25%,” he said. The latest figure is, however, still above the national target of 125 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births. The region also recorded an increase in live births, from 64,155 in the first half of 2025 to 67,565 during the corresponding period in 2026. Dr Adomako-Boateng said the reduction was partly linked to an expansion of the capacity of peripheral health facilities to manage complicated pregnancies and deliveries. He said Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH), the region’s major referral facility, recorded a decline in its share of maternal deaths, from 62% in 2025 to 54% in 2026. Over the same period, the proportion recorded at facilities outside KATH increased from 28% to 46%. “For the first time in 10 years, Komfo Anokye has reduced the least referral and admissions when it comes to maternal issues. The periphery is relatively handling cases that hitherto would have been referred to KATH.” The development follows efforts by the Regional Health Directorate to strengthen the capacity of lower-level facilities to manage high-risk cases and reduce avoidable referrals. Recent regional interventions have included clinical mentorship involving specialists from KATH and frontline health workers at peripheral facilities. The Directorate has also introduced a virtual labour ward to connect frontline health workers with specialists during complex or high-risk deliveries. Dr Adomako-Boateng said the data also showed that most of the maternal deaths recorded in the region involved women whose cases originated within Ashanti. He said 88.2% of the deaths in the period under review originated within the region, while 8.8% came from outside the region. He said the figures had implications for how maternal healthcare interventions should be designed and implemented across the region. The Regional Health Director credited partners, including UNICEF, for supporting efforts to improve the capacity of health workers. “We have to sustain this gain by continuing building the capacity of nurses, doctors, certified registered anaesthetists through the clinical mentorship intervention with huge support from UNICEF. Thank you, UNICEF.” The Ashanti Region also recorded a decline in its institutional stillbirth rate, falling from 6.52 to 6.08 per 1,000 live births, according to figures presented at the review. Ashanti Regional Minister Dr Frank Amoakohene welcomed the improvement but stressed that the maternal mortality ratio remained above the national target. “We have fallen from a whopping 199 per 100,000 live births to 148 per 100,000 live births.” He commended the Regional Health Directorate but said further work was needed to bring the figure down to the national target of 125 deaths per 100,000 live births. Dr Amoakohene also highlighted government interventions aimed at expanding access to healthcare, including funding for the completion of the KNUST Medical Centre and the rollout of Free Primary Healthcare. Eight districts, including Sekyere Central and Amansie South, have been earmarked for the first phase of the Free Primary Healthcare rollout in the region. The initiative is expected to help address gaps in access to primary healthcare, while the Regional Health Directorate continues to explore measures to ensure that complex pregnancy cases are identified and managed earlier at peripheral facilities.

items.title: Ghana’s unemployment situation is ‘scary’ – NSA Ashanti regional Director
items.description: The Ashanti Regional Director of the National Service Authority (NSA), Emmanuel Fynn Reagan, has described Ghana’s unemployment situation as “scary,” warning that urgent measures are needed to address the growing challenge. He said the number of young people entering the job market each year far exceeds the number of available jobs, making it necessary to equip graduates with skills that can enable them to create their own employment. Speaking to the media on Thursday, September 17, Mr Fynn Reagan said the National Service Authority had a role to play in addressing the challenge by going beyond its traditional mandate of deploying graduates for national service. “The unemployment situation in the country is very scary and if proper measures are not taken, it will lead to a different thing else,” he said. “So we in National Service, we are also there to shape the economy. We are also there to transform the economy.” According to him, many graduates struggle to secure employment after completing their national service, leaving them moving from one place to another in search of jobs. “Most of the time what we see is that people complete their National Service, and you see them moving around everywhere looking, seeking jobs,” he said. Mr Fynn Reagan questioned whether the country had enough jobs to absorb the growing number of young people entering the labour market each year. “The question is how many jobs can absorb the teeming youth that comes out every year?” he asked. Skills training He said the National Service Authority had therefore decided to complement its core mandate by providing graduates with skills training to improve their ability to earn a living independently. He explained that the initiative was intended to equip young people with practical skills that could enable them to establish businesses when they are unable to secure formal employment. “That is giving them skill training and so that when they are done, they can do something on their own,” he said. Mr Fynn Reagan said empowering graduates to establish small businesses could also help create additional employment opportunities for others. He noted that graduates who successfully establish and grow their businesses could become entrepreneurs and employers themselves, contributing to efforts to reduce unemployment. “If they are done and they have no chance on any employment, through the small businesses they can also create their own businesses, become business tycoons, become entrepreneurs, to employ others as well,” he said. Mr Fynn Reagan said such an approach would help address the unemployment challenge by shifting some young people from job seekers to job creators. “This is the only way we can reduce the unemployment situation in the country,” he said.

items.title: Dickson restates commitment to multi-party democracy
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, has reiterated his commitment to multi-party democracy and a peaceful political process ahead of the 2027 general elections. Dickson spoke when the management of LEADERSHIP Newspaper, led by its Vice Chairman, Mr Michael Okpere, paid him a formal visit at his Abuja residence to present notification of his selection as the newspaper’s Politician of the Year 2026. LEADERSHIP had earlier announced Dickson, who represents Bayelsa West in the Senate, as the recipient of the honour, citing his public service record, political leadership and role in the emergence of the NDC as a new opposition platform. Receiving the delegation, the former Bayelsa State governor expressed appreciation to the management and board of the newspaper for the recognition and the process through which the selection was made. Dickson said neither he nor members of his political team had prior knowledge of the nomination, adding that he was surprised when the announcement was made public. He commended LEADERSHIP for what he described as the integrity and independence demonstrated in the award process, saying the honour was not a personal achievement but one that belonged to the NDC’s leadership, members and supporters. Dickson dedicated the award to party officials and members at all levels, including those at the local government and ward levels, for their contributions to the development of the party. He also dedicated the honour to Nigerians at home and abroad who, according to him, believe in the NDC’s vision and its stated commitment to strengthening the country’s democratic space. Dickson said the emergence of the NDC followed difficult political decisions and a determination to pursue a different political direction. He said he chose not to remain in what he considered an ineffective opposition structure and also declined to join the ruling party or the African Democratic Congress (ADC). According to him, establishing a new political platform required conviction, sacrifice and the support of Nigerians and political associates who believed in the project. He acknowledged the support of the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and former Kano State Governor, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, whom he said had expressed confidence in the political project. Dickson said the NDC had continued to grow through the collective efforts of its leadership, members and supporters across the country. He used the occasion to reiterate the party’s commitment to multi-party democracy and a peaceful electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. Dickson called on political actors and relevant institutions to ensure that Nigerians are able to campaign and express their political choices freely and without intimidation or violence. “We are not enemies. We are fellow Nigerians who disagree,” he said, stressing that political differences should not become a basis for violence or restrictions on citizens’ democratic rights. He also called on President Bola Tinubu to lead efforts to de-escalate political tensions and ensure that security agencies provide a conducive environment for political parties and candidates to campaign across the country. The NDC leader said the party would engage relevant security agencies ahead of its nationwide campaign activities to seek adequate security for its candidates, officials and supporters. items.title: Éliminatoires CAN 2027 : Amir Abdou convoque 25 Étalons sans Bertrand Traoré
items.description: Le sélectionneur des Étalons du Burkina Faso, Amir Abdou, a dévoilé, ce jeudi 17 septembre 2026, la liste des joueurs convoqués pour les deux premières journées des éliminatoires de la Coupe d’Afrique des Nations (CAN) 2027 le 25 septembre 2026 au Stade du 4-Août face au Bénin, le 28 septembre 2026 face à la Centrafrique à Casablanca au Maroc. Aussi, le match amical contre l'Argentine le 3 octobre 2026 à Buenos Aires en Argentine est au programme. Au total, 25 joueurs ont été retenus, avec sept nouveaux visages dans le groupe. Pour ces premières échéances face au Bénin et à la République centrafricaine, Amir Abdou a décidé d’apporter du sang neuf à son effectif. Plusieurs cadres de la sélection sont toutefois présents, notamment le gardien Hervé Koffi, Edmond Tapsoba, Issa Kaboré et Dango Ouattara. La principale surprise de cette liste reste l’absence de Bertrand Traoré. Le capitaine des Étalons, qui vient de rejoindre Wolverhampton après plusieurs semaines à la recherche d’un nouveau club, n’a pas été retenu pour ces deux rencontres. Pour Amir Abdou, cette absence s’explique notamment par la nécessité de laisser au joueur le temps de retrouver progressivement son rythme. « Bertrand, il faut le laisser prendre ses marques, c’est le capitaine. Il a joué 15 minutes hier. J’étais le plus heureux de le voir sur le terrain. J’ai eu pas mal d’échanges avec lui avant qu’il n’aille dans son club, pendant sa préparation individuelle. Je l’ai félicité pour son nouveau club. Mais il faut lui laisser le temps d’être performant. C’est un joueur important, on sait ce qu’il peut apporter à l’équipe nationale. Je suis content qu’il ait trouvé un projet. Il aurait pu prendre des destinations plus exotiques, mais il est resté dans un championnat très difficile, qui est la Championship. Il y a 24 équipes et elles jouent tous les trois ou quatre jours, donc c’est bien pour lui. Il est parti dans un club ambitieux. Ce sont des clubs qui jouent en Premier League » , a expliqué Amir Abdou. Cette nouvelle liste est également marquée par l’arrivée de sept nouveaux joueurs. En défense, Mamoutou Ouédraogo, évoluant au Sheriff, et Ismaël Maïga, sociétaire du FK Cukaricki, connaissent leur première convocation avec les Étalons. Dans l’entrejeu, Amir Abdou a fait appel à Rachid Kouda de Mantova, Julien Bationo de Streda Dunajska, Axel Taonsa de Västerås SK et Bebel Doumbia de Rapid Bucas. Aboubacar Sidiki Camara, du RB Salzbourg, complète la liste des nouveaux venus et renforce le secteur offensif. Pour le sélectionneur, cette évolution de l’effectif doit permettre aux Étalons de franchir un nouveau cap. Amir Abdou compte notamment sur l’état d’esprit du groupe pour aborder les prochaines échéances dans de bonnes conditions. « Je pense que cette équipe va pouvoir être beaucoup plus performante. Avec l'état d'esprit qu'on va insuffler, ce sera du positif. Je suis confiant pour la suite (…) Le cas de Cyriaque, c’était jusqu’à hier soir. Le joueur a décidé de passer son permis. (…) J’ai échangé avec le Président. Il faut respecter l’équipe nationale. Moi, j’ai un groupe à gérer. Personne n’est irremplaçable (…) Soit vous êtes là pour un projet du début jusqu’à la fin. Le débat est clos. C’est un choix, j’assume mes responsabilités », a souligné le sélectionneur. Avec cette liste renouvelée, les Étalons s’apprêtent donc à lancer leur campagne dans les éliminatoires de la CAN 2027. L’absence du capitaine Bertrand Traoré et l’intégration de sept nouveaux joueurs constituent les principales nouveautés de ce premier groupe dévoilé par Amir Abdou. items.title: 3 Samsung phones that can compete with iPhone 18 Pro
items.description: Apple has raised the bar with the new iPhone 18 Pro, but Samsung has several flagship smartphones capable of going head-to-head with Apple’s latest Pro model. The iPhone 18 Pro comes with Apple’s new A20 Pro chip, a 6.3-inch OLED display, a 48MP triple-camera system and a new variable-aperture main camera. Apple has also introduced improvements to battery life, video recording and sustained performance. However, Samsung’s 2026 smartphone lineup offers alternatives with powerful processors, high-resolution cameras, 120Hz displays, advanced AI features, long-term software support and, in the case of its foldables, form factors Apple does not offer in a conventional Pro phone. Here are three Samsung phones that can compete with the iPhone 18 Pro. 1. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra The Galaxy S26 Ultra is Samsung’s most direct conventional rival to the iPhone 18 Pro. It features a 6.9-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display with a 120Hz refresh rate and Quad HD+ resolution. It also weighs 214g, putting it only slightly above the 211g iPhone 18 Pro despite having a significantly larger screen. Samsung gives the S26 Ultra a 200MP main camera alongside 50MP ultra-wide, 50MP telephoto and 10MP telephoto cameras. Its zoom system includes 3x and 5x optical zoom, as well as up to 100x digital zoom. The phone can also record 8K video. The iPhone 18 Pro, meanwhile, uses three 48MP cameras and introduces a variable-aperture 48MP main camera, allowing users to select different aperture settings for greater control over exposure and depth of field. Samsung also gives the S26 Ultra a 5,000mAh battery, S Pen support and Samsung DeX, turning the phone into a more PC-like productivity device when connected to a compatible display. For buyers comparing the two, the key difference is that Samsung puts greater emphasis on display size, zoom flexibility, stylus input and productivity, while Apple’s Pro model focuses heavily on its A20 Pro-powered performance and camera system. 2. Samsung Galaxy S26 The standard Galaxy S26 is another Samsung phone worth considering against the iPhone 18 Pro, particularly for users who want a smaller flagship. The Galaxy S26 has a 6.3-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display with a 120Hz refresh rate, matching the iPhone 18 Pro’s 6.3-inch screen size. It is also substantially lighter at 167g, compared with 211g for Apple’s phone. Its camera setup consists of a 50MP main camera, 10MP telephoto and 12MP ultra-wide camera. Samsung provides 3x optical zoom and up to 30x digital zoom, while the phone can record 8K video. The S26 also packs a 4,300mAh battery and supports Samsung DeX. Samsung lists up to 30 hours of video playback for the device, although battery claims from different manufacturers should not be treated as directly comparable because testing methods can differ. The iPhone 18 Pro has more advanced Pro-level camera hardware, including three 48MP cameras and variable aperture on its main camera. But the Galaxy S26 offers a compact 6.3-inch 120Hz flagship experience in a considerably lighter body. 3. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 The Galaxy Z Fold8 takes a different approach to competing with Apple’s Pro lineup. Rather than trying to imitate the conventional smartphone design, Samsung turns the phone into a foldable device that can function as both a smartphone and a larger tablet-like screen. The Z Fold8 has a 5.5-inch cover display and a 7.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X main display when opened. Both screens support refresh rates of up to 120Hz. The device weighs 201g and measures only 4.5mm thick when unfolded. Samsung equips the Fold8 with a 4,800mAh battery and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor. Storage options include 256GB, 512GB and 1TB. Its rear camera system includes dual 50MP cameras, while Samsung says the phone can record 8K video. It also supports Samsung DeX, giving the Fold8 additional productivity capabilities beyond those of a conventional smartphone. The iPhone 18 Pro remains a traditional 6.3-inch smartphone, while the Fold8 can transform into a much larger 7.6-inch display. That makes Samsung’s foldable particularly relevant to consumers who prioritise multitasking, large-screen content consumption and mobile productivity. items.title: US Revokes Limits on Power Plants’ Climate Pollution
items.description: Click to expand Image Pollution and steam are seen rising from the stacks of the Miami Fort Power Station along the Ohio River, in North Bend, Ohio, on July 23, 2026. © 2026 Jason Whitman/NurPhoto via AP Photo The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced on September 14 that it is repealing limits on climate-warming pollution from coal and gas-fired power plants, the second largest source of greenhouse gas emissions in the country. By gutting the 2024 Carbon Pollution Standards, the EPA is eliminating most of the limits on power plants’ carbon emissions. The move is one of the Trump administration’s most significant attacks yet on the US government’s ability to confront the climate crisis and protect communities devastated by pollution. The 2024 standards required existing coal plants and new gas plants to capture 90 percent of carbon emissions or shut down by 2039, which would have reduced carbon pollution by an estimated 1.38 billion metric tons through 2047. The Biden-era rule was also projected to help reduce power plants’ emissions of health-harming pollutants, including sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, and fine particulate matter. Human Rights Watch has documented how these pollutants from industrial operations can degrade air quality and harm the health of communities living nearby. Our research in countries like Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Türkiye has shown how coal-fired plants, in particular, can emit pollution that contributes to dangerous levels of air pollution. The Biden administration estimated that the 2024 Carbon Standards would prevent 1,200 deaths and 360,000 asthma attacks in the US in 2035 alone. The EPA claimed its repeal of the 2024 standards would save businesses $370 million in regulatory costs but did not say what the costs to public health would be. In January, the agency said it would no longer factor in health costs when estimating the economic impact of pollution limits. In its announcement rescinding the 2024 carbon standards, the EPA also proposed removing “all remaining greenhouse gas emissions requirements for power plants,” arguing these emissions do not impact climate change. In 2025, the agency also revoked its 2009 finding that greenhouse gases endanger public health, a finding grounded in scientific evidence that had provided a legal foundation for federal regulation of greenhouse gas emissions. While the Trump administration mounts a full-throated denial of decades of scientific evidence, communities across the country—and the world—are already contending with the consequences of the climate crisis. The EPA should restore the 2024 standards and strengthen its regulation of the fossil fuel industry.

items.title: Burkina : La « Nuit de la RPP » se tiendra le 30 septembre 2026
items.description: La « Nuit de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP) » se tiendra le 30 septembre 2026, sous le slogan « Le Peuple veille sur sa Révolution ». L’annonce a été faite, ce jeudi 17 septembre 2026, lors d’une conférence de presse consacrée à cet événement, qui s’inscrit dans le cadre de la célébration du quatrième anniversaire de l’accession au pouvoir du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. La « Nuit de la RPP » se tiendra le 30 septembre 2026. Selon le président du comité d’organisation, Sougrinoma Ibrahim Guigma, cette nuit vise à réaffirmer la souveraineté nationale, à renforcer la ferveur révolutionnaire et à favoriser la communion populaire. Elle sera également l’occasion de présenter les réalisations et les acquis enregistrés dans le cadre de la RPP, à travers des images, des chiffres, des témoignages et des capsules sectorielles. Le Président du comité d'organisation Sougrinoma Ibrahim Guigma Prévue de 18 h à 2 h du matin, la manifestation s’articulera autour de trois séquences. La première, de 18 h à 20 h, sera consacrée à un spectacle d’installation et de maintien. La deuxième, de 20 h à minuit, prendra la forme d’une partie officielle dédiée à la présentation des acquis de la RPP. La troisième, un grand concert de la révolution, clôturera la soirée jusqu’à 2 h. Des artistes nationaux et internationaux sont annoncés, issus notamment de la musique, du slam, de l’humour, de la danse et des arts dramatiques. 30 septembre 2022 – 30 septembre 2026 : 4 ans d'exercice du pouvoir par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré Le président du comité d’organisation a précisé que la célébration se déroulera simultanément dans les chefs-lieux de régions ainsi que dans les ambassades et représentations diplomatiques du Burkina Faso.
