items.title: Dakar : 51 personnes concernées par cinq procédures d’information judiciaire
items.description: Le procureur de la République près le Tribunal de grande instance hors classe de Dakar a fait le point sur plusieurs procédures judiciaires ouvertes entre mars et juillet 2026. Dans un communiqué de presse, il indique que cinq procédures d’information judiciaire ont été ouvertes et confiées aux juges des premier et quatrième cabinets d’instruction. Ces procédures portent sur des faits qualifiés de viol, pédophilie, détournement de mineurs, actes contre nature avec un individu du même sexe, transmission volontaire du VIH/Sida et mise en danger de la vie d’autrui, selon le parquet. Au total, 51 personnes sont concernées par ces procédures. Parmi elles, 49 sont actuellement placées en détention provisoire, tandis que deux autres sont sous contrôle judiciaire. 33 personnes renvoyées devant les juridictions de jugement Le parquet précise par ailleurs que 14 personnes ont fait l’objet d’un renvoi devant la Chambre criminelle, tandis que 19 autres ont été renvoyées devant la Chambre correctionnelle. Parquet de Dakar : 51 personnes poursuivies dans cinq procédures judiciaires Ces décisions concernent donc 33 personnes, dont les dossiers sont désormais appelés à être examinés par les juridictions de jugement compétentes. Deux procédures toujours en cours Les deux dernières procédures, qui impliquent 18 personnes, sont toujours en cours d’instruction, précise le communiqué du procureur de la République. Le parquet ne donne pas, dans ce document, davantage de détails sur l’identité des personnes concernées ni sur les circonstances précises des faits reprochés. Les procédures judiciaires se poursuivent donc à différents stades, entre instruction et renvoi devant les juridictions de jugement.

items.title: Constitutional Review: 5-year term means extra year to amass wealth, loot state coffers — Ansa-Asare
items.description: Former Director of the Ghana School of Law, Kweku Ansa-Asare, has rejected the proposed extension of Ghana’s presidential term from four to five years, describing the move as unnecessary. According to him, a president who cannot deliver within the existing four-year mandate should not seek the presidency in the first place. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Thursday, September 17, Mr Ansa-Asare said he was disappointed with what he described as the government’s decision to fast-track the constitutional review process. “My initial reaction is one of disappointment in a sense that the government appears to have fast-tracked the process beyond our imagination,” he said. He said the timing of the proposed constitutional changes was particularly concerning because 2028 is an election year. “The government is aware that 2028 is an election year, and if it puts in place the process for referendum and all that, it is likely to hit into the election year and go beyond the election,” he said. Mr Ansa-Asare said he was opposed to the proposed five-year presidential term because, in his view, it could create opportunities for abuse of public resources. “I have already made my position clear on the five-year presidential term: that it is another way of corruption to enable the president to amass wealth, loot state coffers and all that,” he said. He argued that extending the mandate would give elected officials an additional year in office without necessarily improving their ability to deliver on their responsibilities. “Already, in the four years, we have seen the corrupt practices of government functionaries. And if we are to extend by another year, by the time we get to another amendment in, say, 20 years’ time, which will increase the term from five years to, say, ten years, we will have no state coffers in this country,” he said. Mr Ansa-Asare maintained that four years should be sufficient for a president to implement their programme. “I am opposed to the five years, because if anyone who decides to conduct a presidential election cannot function within four years, then the president has no business entering the race at all,” he said. He also criticised the practice of presidents and governments taking time after assuming office to develop their policy plans. “You don’t have to wait until you win, and then you use one year to gather the blueprint for your minister, instead of you to do that before you can get into office,” he said. “On principle, I’m totally against the five years,” he added.

items.title: Bekwai MP rewards top BECE performers as academic results improve
items.description: Member of Parliament for Bekwai, Ralph Poku-Adusei, has rewarded outstanding Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) candidates in the constituency under his School Starter-Pack Scholarship (SSPS) programme. The initiative, introduced to address concerns over declining academic performance in the Bekwai Municipality, provides merit-based support to top-performing students from public and private schools. Five students were recognised as the overall best performers in the 2026 edition. Miss Owusu Adwoa Serwaa of Dominase M/A JHS, who obtained Aggregate 7, was named Overall Best Female Student from a public school, while Master Yamoah Bordom Benjamin of Bekwai APS JHS, with Aggregate 8, was named Overall Best Male Student from a public school. From the private schools category, Miss Appiah Kubi Annabella and Master Frimpong Owusu Emmanuel, both of Amazing Grace JHS, were recognised as the Overall Best Female and Male Students, respectively, after obtaining Aggregate 6. Master Kingsley Owusu of Dominase M/A JHS was also recognised as the Best Student with a disability (PWD). Each of the five overall winners received a laptop, Mackintosh mattress, plastic provibox, pillow and suitcase. The PWD beneficiary will additionally receive a GH¢2,000-per-term educational scholarship from the MP throughout his Senior High School education. The SSPS also provides a boarding starter pack comprising a mattress, pillow, plastic provibox and suitcase to the best graduating candidate from every public and private school in each community. The beneficiaries are selected by the Bekwai Municipal Education Directorate based on their BECE aggregates. Where students record the same aggregate, their raw scores are used to determine the beneficiary. Mr Poku-Adusei said the programme was designed as a merit-based intervention to motivate students to pursue academic excellence rather than as a conventional donation scheme. The SSPS was introduced alongside the reintroduction of the School Performance Appraisal Meeting (SPAM), which the MP funded across all 10 educational circuits in the constituency. A stakeholder engagement held in early 2025 identified parental apathy, teacher motivation and supervision gaps, student indiscipline, inadequate teaching and learning materials, and limited academic competition among factors affecting educational outcomes. Mr Poku-Adusei said improving education required more than infrastructure, stressing the importance of motivation, accountability and a supportive learning environment. He has also announced a Best Teacher Awards Scheme, which is currently being finalised. A dedicated SSPS Board has been established to oversee the programme, including its selection criteria, benefits and transparency measures. The MP said he wanted the initiative to continue beyond his tenure and eventually attract support from individuals and corporate organisations to extend its reach. He said the long-term goal was to support beneficiaries through Senior High School and tertiary education and help produce professionals who would contribute to the development of the Bekwai constituency.

items.title: Hardship: Bagudu’s admission vindicates us — APM
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Allied Peoples Movement, APM, said Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Senator Abubakar Bagudu’s admission that the Tinubu administration failed to anticipate the scale of economic turbulence confronting Nigeria vindicated its earlier warnings about the government’s policies. The party said the admission was coming as Nigerians grapple with rising living costs, business closures, unemployment and worsening poverty, which it attributed to the administration’s economic reforms. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Abubakar Yusuf, the APM said Bagudu’s remarks at the Federal Appointees Strategic Summit in Abuja on Wednesday confirmed its position that the government lacked adequate economic foresight and safeguards. “Bagudu’s admission at the Federal Appointees Strategic Summit in Abuja on Wednesday that the Tinubu administration did not anticipate what it described as the scale of turbulence that hit the global economy is a gross admission of incompetence which also validates our position that the Tinubu Government lacked the coherent economic blueprint, policy foresight and adequate safeguards required to manage a nation,” the party said. The APM said it had warned against the removal of fuel subsidy, floating of the naira, increased taxes and other policies, alleging that the government ignored the consequences for citizens and businesses. “Right from the onset, well-meaning Nigerians had cautioned that the abrupt removal of subsidy on petroleum products, floating of the Naira, imposition of harsh taxes and other anti-production policies in an economy such as Nigeria would precipitate untold hardship on the people,” it said. It alleged that multinational companies had exited Nigeria, businesses had folded, and millions of Nigerians were struggling to afford food, medication and other basic necessities, while corruption and treasury looting persisted. The party consequently called on President Tinubu to accept responsibility, apologise to Nigerians and withdraw from the 2027 presidential race. “Now that the administration has admitted that it has failed and that it is responsible for the woes of the citizens, it is expected that President Tinubu should take responsibility, apologize to Nigerians and quit the 2027 Presidential race,” Yusuf said. The APM also called for what it described as a “hard reset” of the country, saying Nigeria needed leadership with a clear economic blueprint, policy foresight and safeguards for citizens. It urged Nigerians to support its presidential candidate, Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, whom the party said had a roadmap for tackling the nation’s economic and security challenges, citing his record in Oyo State as a model it wants replicated nationally. The party said it would continue mobilising Nigerians ahead of the January 19, 2027 presidential election to “democratically take back Nigeria from the misrule of the APC”. items.title: Yémen : « Plus de 12 millions d’enfants menacés par la reprise des hostilités »
items.description: Dans un communiqué de presse publié ce mercredi 16 septembre, l’UNICEF estime à 12 millions le nombre d’enfants menacés par la reprise des hostilités au Yémen. La reprise des combats dans le sud du Golfe, au Yémen, menace des millions d’enfants, selon un communiqué de l’UNICEF publié ce mercredi 16 septembre. Le pays traverse une « crise humanitaire déjà extrêmement sévère », qui a entraîné le déplacement de 57 000 enfants en l’espace de deux semaines. « D’autres sont tués, blessés ou portés disparus », souligne l’agence des Nations unies chargée de la protection de l’enfance. D’après l’UNICEF, « au moins neuf enfants auraient été tués et 12 autres blessés, tandis que trois enfants restent portés disparus ». « Les enfants au Yémen vivaient déjà l’une des crises humanitaires les plus graves au monde, et nombre d’entre eux n’ont connu que les conflits et les déplacements », a déclaré Edouard Beigbeder, directeur régional de l’UNICEF pour le Moyen-Orient et l’Afrique du Nord. L’agence rappelle qu’avant cette nouvelle escalade, elle estimait à 12,2 millions le nombre d’enfants ayant besoin d’une aide humanitaire au Yémen. Elle indique également que « plus de 2,2 millions d’enfants de moins de 5 ans souffrent de malnutrition aiguë ». Les tensions dans le pays sont ravivées par le conflit opposant les Houthis aux forces gouvernementales yéménites. Les Houthis, soutenus par l’Iran, contestent la légitimité du pouvoir en place, dirigé par un gouvernement soutenu par l’Arabie saoudite. Boubacar DIOP (stagiaire)

items.title: Mahama directs inter-agency task force to submit roadmap to deal with drug trafficking in two weeks
items.description: President John Mahama has directed the formation of an inter-agency task force to develop a detailed roadmap on measures to prevent the trafficking of drugs through Ghana’s borders. The task force has been given two weeks to present the roadmap, which will be based on recommendations from an urgent meeting chaired by the President with security chiefs and Ministers at the Jubilee House. The President was briefed that ten individuals, including four officers of the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority, are currently being held as investigations continue. The meeting also recommended new actions to strengthen the country’s systems for preventing narcotics trafficking. The meeting follows the seizure by French customs of nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine, valued at about €225 million, at the northern port of Dunkirk on September 10. The cocaine was concealed in a container carrying plastic waste that had arrived from Ghana, with part of the shipment reportedly destined for Antwerp, Belgium. French authorities have opened an investigation into the consignment and the criminal network allegedly behind it, while Ghanaian authorities have also begun investigations into how the shipment left the country. Four suspects were remanded into police custody this week. READ ALSO: Ghana calls for stronger regional cooperation to combat drug trafficking The Presidency said the meeting “reviewed the structure and security systems in place and recommended new actions” to strengthen efforts to prevent the movement of narcotics through Ghana’s borders. Under the President’s directive, the inter-agency task force is expected to present its detailed roadmap within two weeks. The proposals will be based on the findings and recommendations arising from the security meeting. “The President was informed that ten (10) individuals, including four officers of the Customs Division of the GRA are being held while investigations continue,” the statement said.

items.title: Gender Ministry tasks women in media to drive Affirmative Action Act implementation
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection has called on women in the media to play a leading role in educating the public, monitoring compliance and keeping institutions accountable for the implementation of the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024 (Act 1121). The call was made at a capacity-building workshop organised by the Ministry for Women in the media on Thursday, September 17. The workshop sought to improve participants’ understanding of the Act and strengthen their ability to report accurately, fairly and sensitively on gender equity issues. The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, said the media had taken on a responsibility that was central to the Ministry’s work. “I just want you to know that you have taken on a responsibility which is at the heart of everything we do, which is at the centre of everything we do,” she said. According to her, the passage of the law had shifted the focus from advocacy for affirmative action legislation to ensuring that the law was effectively implemented and produced results. “The issue of affirmative action, like many laws and policies we are having in the ministry, has moved from advocating for a law to the law being there and seeing to its effective implementation,” she said. “What we want to see is the impact.” Dr Lartey said the workshop was organised deliberately to bring women in the media into the implementation process and encourage them to champion the cause of greater representation of women in leadership. She said the issue should not be seen as one concerning women alone, but as a national development matter requiring the involvement of men and other stakeholders. “It is not about an individual, it is not about a group of people, it is not about one of the sexes, it is about the nation,” she said. “It is about the country Ghana that is dear to us. If two sexes make up the nation, we cannot grow or develop with just one sex being at the helm of our affairs.” Dr Lartey said the Ministry wanted the media to help bring the implementation of the Act closer to the public, including at the community level, while also drawing international attention to Ghana’s efforts to promote women in leadership. “We are humbled that you’ve taken on this great responsibility to make sure that the Affirmative Action Act is translated into real action where Ghanaians and those it’s meant to serve will actually feel it,” she said. Dr Lartey acknowledged that more work was needed to increase women’s representation, particularly in elected political positions. She pointed to Parliament and local government as areas where the country still needed to make progress. The Minister said the timing of elections made it particularly important for stakeholders to act early, because opportunities to increase women’s representation in elected positions could not simply be created outside the electoral cycle. “When you miss one, especially in the political space, it’s difficult to catch up,” she said. “You can do with appointments, but when it comes to the elected positions, they have periods within which elections take place.” She also said public education was necessary because some women could become accustomed to existing arrangements when they did not see alternative possibilities. “Sometimes when you don’t see the options so clearly, you become so comfortable with what you see because it becomes the norm,” she said. She said exposing women and girls to other possibilities could help them become more aware of their potential contribution to society. The Minister assured the participants that the Ministry was prepared to work with them and other stakeholders to translate the law into practical outcomes. “The ministry is prepared to work with you every step of the way, all other stakeholders on board, to make sure that we translate this law into reality for every woman, every man in Ghana,” she said. “Because when the women stand better, the men also enjoy better. And our children are the end beneficiaries of it all.” The Chief Director of the Ministry, Dr Mariam W.A. Kpakpah, said the Ministry had a mandate to ensure that both state and non-state actors understood the purpose of the Act and their responsibilities under it. She said the Ministry had therefore begun a series of sensitisation and dissemination activities, with women in the media being targeted because of their ability to reach a wider audience. “As women in media, you first of all are a woman yourself, and so you understand the issues of gender,” she said. “But more importantly, you are also a media practitioner, and you’ll be able to put the information out there, let people understand what their role is in implementing the Act, and be able to also bring to the Ministry issues and concerns that we may be able to take forward.” Dr Kpakpah said the Act required 30 per cent representation of women in public institutions and on boards, as well as within private institutions. “We are all supposed to have 30% representation of women in public institutions, on boards, even within private institutions,” she said. She added that the Ministry would monitor implementation and collect information from stakeholders at the end of the year. “At the end of the year, the Ministry will go round, and we will collect information from all stakeholders. We will also issue certificates at the end of the year, to be able to see where we are, how we progress,” she said. She urged women in the media to help disseminate information about the Act and also serve as a channel through which concerns about its implementation could be brought to the Ministry. The Chair of the African Women Leaders Network (AWLN), Dr Charity Binka, said the passage of the Affirmative Action Act was the result of years of advocacy and should not be taken for granted. She said the journey towards the law had taken 13 years, with sustained efforts to push the affirmative action agenda before the legislation was finally passed in 2024. “It took us 13 years to get to where we are today,” she said. Dr Binka said the law should not be viewed simply as legislation for women, but as a development tool aimed at addressing barriers to women’s participation in decision-making. “This is not just a favour to women. People think it’s a women thing, but it’s not. It is a development tool,” she said. She said the law’s implementation was now the major challenge, particularly in achieving its targets for women’s representation. “The passage of the Act was indeed an important milestone because we can work with it. At least it gives us structure,” she said. “However, passing a law is different from living it. Implementation is where many laws fail and where the media must not fail.”

items.title: MoFA launches National Horticultural Seed Roadmap to improve access to quality seeds
items.description: The Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) has launched the National Horticultural Seed Roadmap as part of efforts to strengthen Ghana’s seed system and improve farmers’ access to quality seeds and seedlings. The roadmap, launched in Accra on Thursday, September 17, 2026, provides a strategic framework for the development of the horticultural seed sector over the next three to five years. It focuses on increasing the availability, accessibility and adoption of improved planting materials that are suited to Ghana’s local conditions. Speaking at the launch, Deputy Minister for Food and Agriculture, John Setor Dumelo, described the roadmap as an important step towards building a stronger and more responsive seed system capable of meeting the needs of farmers and supporting growth in horticulture. Implementation of the roadmap will focus on strengthening local seed production and enterprises, expanding farmers’ access to quality seeds and seedlings, and supporting the development of crop varieties adapted to Ghanaian conditions. It will also establish clear responsibilities, timelines and financing arrangements to guide implementation. The Netherlands Embassy, represented by Inge Tenniglo, reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Ghana’s horticultural seed sector. She described the initiative as “laying the foundation for the future of Ghana’s horticulture sector.” The launch brought together representatives from government, the seed industry, research institutions, farmer organisations and development partners, providing a platform for stakeholders to align their efforts towards improving Ghana’s horticultural seed value chain.

items.title: Anambra auto makers hail FG local vehicle policy
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Two automobile manufacturers in Anambra State, Innoson Vehicle Manufacturing (IVM), Nnewi, and Jojo Motors Auto Assembly, Umunya, have welcomed the Federal Government’s new policy making it mandatory for Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) to patronise locally manufactured vehicles. Officials of the two companies spoke during a visit by members of the board of the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC) to their facilities in Anambra. They said the policy would provide greater opportunities for local manufacturers and increase patronage of their products. Managing Director of Innoson Vehicle Manufacturing, Chief Innocent Chukwuma, said he was particularly encouraged by the Federal Government’s emphasis on Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), which he described as an important opportunity for the Nigerian automobile industry. Chukwuma said his company had dedicated its newest facility to the production of CNG-powered trucks and electric vehicles in support of the government’s CNG initiative. “President Bola Tinubu visited some countries and saw the benefits of CNG and on his return, he began to support it. From the president’s plan, by next year, there will be CNG plants in all parts of the country because a lot of money has been invested in it,” he said. He said the rising cost of fuel had made CNG an attractive alternative for motorists and businesses. “With the rising cost of fuel, CNG is the way to go. There is so much gap between the price of diesel and CNG gas and that is why we want everyone to embrace it and move Nigeria forward,” he said. Chukwuma said the company was investing in the automobile sector to create jobs and support families through its operations. “We are investing massively in the automobile industry to make sure that our youths are busy and myself to also be busy. When the factory is constantly working, all categories of people are benefiting,” he said. He commended NADDC for supporting automobile manufacturers across the country but called for greater backward integration to enable companies to specialise in the production of components in which they have comparative advantage. Executive Director of Jojo Motors, Chinedu Oguegbo, said the company was focused on manufacturing commercial vehicles for the Nigerian transportation sector and had begun to benefit from the Federal Government’s local vehicle patronage policy. “We brought the facility to where the customers are,” he said. Oguegbo, however, said the company had faced challenges in recent years, particularly the depreciation and fluctuations in the value of the naira, which he said had made long-term business decisions difficult. He said the company had persevered and was currently in the first phase of its development. “As it is, things are actually stabilising and we believe that the next time the board members come, our gas facility will be ready,” he said. Oguegbo said the company’s major brand, Omma Bus, manufactured at its Umunya facility, could soon be exported, while its natural gas facility was expected to commence operations shortly. Director-General of NADDC, Oluwemimo Joseph, said the visit was aimed at obtaining first-hand information about the needs and challenges of automobile manufacturers. He said the information gathered would assist the council in reviewing policies and contributing to legislation aimed at improving the operating environment in the sector. “We know that those who are into production in Nigeria face a lot of challenges. These challenges will be reduced when we interact with the manufacturers and proffer solutions on how to overcome them,” Joseph said. He said NADDC was also examining opportunities for backward integration by identifying vehicle components that could be manufactured locally. According to him, the council was exploring ways of linking small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Anambra with the automobile industry to enable them supply locally manufactured components. Joseph also said manufacturers had raised concerns about competition from imported used vehicles, adding that the council was taking the concerns to the appropriate authorities. He specifically mentioned issues surrounding duty policies on CNG and electric vehicles. Chairman of NADDC, Chief Emma Eneukwu, said the council was advocating legislation to address what he described as the influx of imported used vehicles into the Nigerian market. He said the development had made it difficult for local vehicle manufacturers to compete effectively. “We will use the law to protect our local producers so that they can easily sell their products. Because some of these imported vehicles are tax free, our local manufacturers cannot effectively compete with them,” Eneukwu said. He also urged local manufacturers to increase the use of locally produced components while improving their capacity to compete in the automobile market. “There could be a few components that could be imported, but we should be able to have our locally manufactured parts that should be used in the manufacture of vehicles,” he said. Eneukwu called for greater patronage of locally manufactured vehicles, saying increased public acceptance would depend partly on the durability and affordability of the products. “I believe that gradually we will get there. But the most important thing is encouragement for our people to stop relying on foreign products and insist on made-in-Nigeria vehicles,” he said. The post Anambra auto makers hail FG local vehicle policy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 10 people, including 4 Customs officers held as Ghana probes drug trafficking through ports
items.description: Ten individuals, including four officers of the Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), are being held as investigations continue into recent drug trafficking through Ghana’s ports. President John Dramani Mahama was informed of the development during an urgent meeting with security chiefs on Thursday, where he received a detailed briefing on investigations into the trafficking of drugs out of the country’s ports. According to a statement issued on Thursday, September 17, by Minister for Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, “ten (10) individuals, including four officers of the Customs Division of the GRA, are being held while investigations continue.” The Presidency did not disclose the identities of those in custody or provide details of the allegations against them. It also did not indicate whether charges had been filed, as the investigations remain ongoing. The alleged involvement of four Customs officers is among the key developments emerging from the case, although no allegation of wrongdoing against any individual has been established in the statement. The meeting also reviewed the existing structures and security systems in place to prevent drug trafficking and considered additional measures to strengthen controls. President Mahama directed the formation of an inter-agency task force to develop a detailed roadmap aimed at preventing the trafficking of drugs through Ghana’s borders. The task force is expected to present its proposals within two weeks, with the roadmap to be based on the outcome of Thursday’s meeting.

items.title: Burkina : Le Gouvernement met en place l’Inspection générale des ressources humaines pour une gestion plus efficace du personnel de l’Administration publique
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 17 septembre 2026). ‎Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a présidé ce jeudi, l’hebdomadaire Conseil des ministres. Selon le Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO, le Conseil a examiné d’importants dossiers et pris des décisions pour répondre aux aspirations profondes du Peuple burkinabè conformément aux orientations de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP). Au titre du ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création et organisation de l'Inspection générale des ressources humaines. Pour le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Camarade Mathias TRAORÉ « la création de l'Inspection générale des ressources humaines s'inscrit dans la dynamique de la transformation profonde de l’administration et conformément aux exigences de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire ». Pour le Ministre TRAORÉ, la Commission de régulation des dysfonctionnements (CRD) a procédé à un diagnostic de l'ensemble des dysfonctionnements de l'Administration publique au cours de l'année 2025. « Il s'est trouvé que les dysfonctionnements qui ont été relevés ne seront pas entièrement couverts par les conseils de discipline qui sont mis en place. Il se trouve aussi que le personnel de l'État constitue des ressources qui sont mises à la disposition des autres administrations », soutient le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple. C’est pourquoi, selon lui, le gouvernement a décidé de la création d’une structure transversale à mesure d'auditer et de contrôler la gestion qui est faite de l'ensemble de ses ressources humaines, y compris celles mises à la disposition des institutions et autres structures publiques. L’Inspection générale des ressources humaines permettra « d'avoir avec précision l'effectif des agents dans l'Administration publique, de contrôler l'utilisation qui est faite de ce personnel et enfin de voir la rémunération qui en découle afin de maîtriser les effectifs et la masse salariale », a soutenu le Ministre. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso

items.title: Guinée : France 24 interdite d’émettre pour avoir qualifié Mamadi Doumbouya de « président putschiste
items.description: La Haute Autorité de la Communication (HAC) guinéenne a rendu publique sa décision n° 032/HAC/P/2026, ce jeudi 17 septembre. Elle porte interdiction de diffusion de la chaîne de télévision « France 24 » sur le territoire de la République de Guinée. La chaîne de télévision « France 24 » est donc interdite de diffusion en Guinée. La décision de la Haute Autorité de la Communication a été rendue publique ce jeudi 17 septembre, après délibération en séance extraordinaire. L'autorité s'est appuyée sur sa précédente décision n° 041/HAC/2026, en date du 16 septembre 2026, par laquelle elle mettait déjà « France 24 » en « demeure formelle », lui intimant l'ordre de « cesser immédiatement l'usage des termes attentatoires à la dignité du Chef de l'État » et de procéder aux « rectifications éditoriales requises ». La HAC a considéré que le « refus manifeste, délibéré et caractérisé » de la direction de la chaîne d'appliquer cette mise en demeure constituait une « insubordination », une « offense continue » à la personne du président de la République guinéenne, Mamadi Doumbouya, mais aussi une « violation flagrante de la souveraineté juridique de la République de Guinée ». Tout est parti d'une édition du journal télévisé diffusée le 15 septembre, au cours de laquelle un présentateur de « France 24 » avait employé l'expression « président putschiste » pour désigner Mamadi Doumbouya. Dans l'article 2 de sa décision, la Haute Autorité de la Communication précise : « L'autorisation de diffusion sur le territoire national est révoquée. Les accréditations de presse de l'ensemble des correspondants, envoyés spéciaux et collaborateurs de la chaîne France 24 en Guinée sont retirées avec effet immédiat. » Dans son article 4, elle ordonne par ailleurs à l'Autorité de Régulation des Postes et Télécommunications (ARPT) le blocage technique, sans délai, de tous les accès numériques de « France 24 ». Boubacar DIOP (stagiaire)

items.title: Cameroun : Madegoua pleure 13 personnes tuées dans une attaque attribuée à Boko Haram
items.description: © DR Dans ce petit village de Madegoua, à 9 km seulement de Makary, dans le Logone-et-Chari, on pensait la nuit paisible. À 2h du matin, dans la nuit du mercredi à ce jeudi 17 septembre, la mort est arrivée à moto. Des hommes armés, que tout le monde là-bas appelle Boko Haram, ont encerclé le village. Ils ont tiré. Sans distinction. Femmes, hommes, vieillards, d’après des témoignages. Ce matin, le sable de Madegoua est rouge. 13 corps gisent au sol. 13 vies arrachées. Des familles entières décimées. Des enfants qui se réveillent orphelins. Et comme si la douleur ne suffisait pas, ces populations meurent déjà à petit feu. La pluie n'est pas venue cette année. Les champs sont secs. Le mil ne pousse plus. Les bêtes peuvent crever de soif. À Madegoua, on ne sait plus de quoi on va mourir : de faim, de soif, ou d'une balle à 2h du matin. Le Logone-et-Chari est à genoux. Les corps des 13 victimes ont été inhumes ce 17 septembre. Cet article Cameroun : Madegoua pleure 13 personnes tuées dans une attaque attribuée à Boko Haram est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Adebutu dares Yayi to go to court over Ekiti indigene claim
items.description: …says Ogun APC in panic mode over PDP’s growing strength By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Oladipupo Adebutu, has challenged the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, to institute legal action against him over claims concerning the senator’s alleged indigene status. Adebutu, a former federal lawmaker, said he was prepared to present documents before a court to substantiate his claim that Adeola was not an indigene of Ogun State. He also accused the ruling APC administration of growing increasingly apprehensive about what he described as the opposition PDP’s growing strength ahead of the 2027 governorship election. Adebutu made the remarks at a PDP campaign rally in Odogbolu Local Government Area. He alleged that PDP campaign billboards were being prevented from being erected while posters belonging to the party were being removed or defaced in parts of the state. The PDP candidate further alleged that the party had initially planned to hold its campaign in Idowa, but was prevented from doing so, prompting the campaign team to relocate the event to Odogbolu. According to him, the alleged restrictions would not stop the PDP from reaching voters across the state. Adebutu said: “the truth is that APC is already jittery; they are in panic mode because they are well aware that the next government in power in the state come 2027 will be the PDP. “They said we can’t have our billboards erected and now they are defacing and removing our posters. Why are they afraid? “They also said that we can’t have our campaign in Idowa, but here we are in Odogbolu, the birthplace of my late mother, Dame Caroline Adebutu.” On the controversy surrounding Adeola’s ancestry, Adebutu said he was ready to face the senator in court if sued over his claim. He said: “It is sad that the APC governorship candidate, Senator Adeola, commonly called Yayi, is threatening to sue people because they said that he is from Ekiti State. “I am daring their lawyers to sue me because the truth is that Yayi is not an indigene of Ogun State. “I am waiting for their lawyer to also sue me so that we can go and present all our documents in the court of law. “They first claimed that they are from Joga, later they said Ishaga, Ilaro and all that. I am waiting for their lawyer to write me so that we can show the whole world the truth.” Adebutu also defended his own claim to Ogun indigene status, saying his mother hailed from Odogbolu while his father, businessman Sir Kensington Adebutu, is from Iperu. He said: “I am a bona fide indigene of Ogun State. My mother was from here in Odogbolu and my father, Sir Kensington Adebutu, is from Iperu, so there is no controversy about where I came from.” The PDP candidate further alleged that Adeola was involved in what he described as “project diversion,” claiming that projects meant for other states had been brought to Ogun State. He also criticised the APC-led government over what he described as poor governance and economic hardship, promising that a PDP administration would prioritise grassroots development, local government autonomy and the welfare of pensioners and workers. “We shall prioritise payment of gratuities of our pensioners. Government workers would have access to their cooperative savings because we won’t touch it; they will always have access to their money to enhance their well-being whenever they want it,” he said. Adebutu also alleged that gunshots were fired at the windscreen and tyres of vehicles in his campaign convoy. At the rally were a former Commissioner for Finance and Director-General of the Oladipupo Adebutu Governorship Campaign, Dr Kehinde Sogunle; former Chairman of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria, ALGON, in the state, Hon. John Obafemi; former Ambassador to Zambia and Malawi, Mrs Folake Marcus-Bello; former Deputy Minority Whip of the ninth National Assembly, Hon. Adesegun Adekoya; the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Alhaja Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo; and other party leaders, aspirants and supporters. Adeola had, in a statement issued on Tuesday by his media aide, Kayode Odunaro, threatened legal action against an APC governorship aspirant, Abayomi Hunye, and Marcus-Bello over what he described as a “libelous declaration on national television” that he was from Ekiti State and not an indigene of Ogun. The senator reportedly gave the individuals 24 hours to provide evidence supporting the claim or face legal action for alleged defamation of character. Speaking at the rally, however, Marcus-Bello said she stood by her claim concerning Adeola’s alleged ancestry, adding that she would make further revelations in the coming weeks. She urged residents to prepare for what she described as a new era of good governance, development and accountability under a PDP administration. The PDP deputy governorship candidate, Sowunmi-Kolapo, also urged residents to turn out with their Permanent Voter Cards and vote for the party in the 2027 election. She said the PDP had developed programmes aimed at improving the living conditions of residents across the state. Obafemi, who recently defected from the APC to the PDP, also called on voters to support Adebutu and the opposition party, arguing that successive APC administrations had subjected residents to hardship since the PDP left power in the state. Meanwhile, the Ogun State chapter of the APC has challenged the allegation by the PDP campaign that gunmen attacked Adebutu’s convoy during its campaign activities. In a statement issued on Thursday by the party’s Publicity Secretary, Femi Nuberu, the APC alleged that the reported shooting was instead carried out by security personnel attached to Adebutu. The party claimed that the incident occurred in Ososa, the hometown of the APC deputy governorship candidate, Mrs Kudirat Abiodun Adegunwa-Balogun. Nuberu called on the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Tunji Disu, to order a thorough and impartial investigation into the incident and ensure that anyone found culpable is held accountable. According to him, the party was concerned about reports that security operatives attached to a governorship candidate allegedly discharged firearms in a populated area. He alleged that Adebutu and his campaign team were returning from Ijebu-Ode when they passed through Ososa and that members of the security team allegedly opened fire and shot sporadically into the air, causing residents and other persons in the area to flee. Nuberu said: “We find it deeply disturbing that security details attached to a candidate seeking to become the governor of Ogun State would reportedly cause apprehension among the populace through the reckless discharge of ammunition. “The incident, which reportedly took place in Ososa, the hometown of our deputy governorship candidate, Mrs Kudirat Abiodun Adegunwa-Balogun, is troubling and must not be allowed to escalate. “It is provocative and capable of creating unnecessary fear and tension among law-abiding citizens. We expect the police investigation to establish the facts surrounding the incident and ensure that anyone found to have acted unlawfully is held accountable.” The APC spokesman also urged Adebutu and his campaign team to exercise restraint and conduct their activities within the law. “We appeal to residents to remain calm, reject retaliation and allow the security agencies to do their work. Political differences must never endanger innocent lives,” he said. The post Adebutu dares Yayi to go to court over Ekiti indigene claim appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La Haute Autorité du Waqf et le PNAMVR signent une convention de partenariat
items.description: La Haute Autorité du Waqf (HAW) et le Programme National d’Aménagement et de Modernisation des Villes Religieuses (PNAMVR) ont signé, ce jeudi 17 septembre 2026 à Dakar, une convention de partenariat destinée à mobiliser le waqf comme instrument de financement du développement des villes religieuses du Sénégal. La convention a été paraphée par le Coordonnateur national du PNAMVR, Amdy Moustapha Mbacké, et par le Directeur général de la HAW, Dr Ahmed Lamine Athie. Un cadre de collaboration structuré Ce partenariat définit un cadre général de collaboration entre les deux institutions autour de la mobilisation et de l’utilisation du waqf comme instrument de financement et de soutien aux projets d’aménagement, de modernisation et de développement durable des villes religieuses. Conclue pour une durée de trois ans renouvelables, la convention prévoit la mise en place d’un Comité Technique Conjoint chargé de la sélection des projets, du suivi technique et financier et de l’évaluation régulière des résultats. Des objectifs partagés Le partenariat s’articule autour de plusieurs axes à savoir promouvoir des financements innovants basés sur le waqf pour garantir l’autonomie financière des projets , faciliter une gouvernance partagée entre acteurs publics, religieux et financiers, dans la transparence ,soutenir la création de pôles d’investissement religieux et communautaire à fort impact social, générateurs d’emplois, de revenus et de services ,pérenniser le patrimoine religieux en intégrant la valorisation du savoir et des valeurs spirituelles et ancrer le modèle waqf comme pilier de la politique publique de développement urbain spirituel. Interrogé à l’issue de la signature, M. Amdy Moustapha Mbacké, Coordonnateur national du PNAMVR, a déclaré : « *Cette convention marque une étape décisive dans la mobilisation de ressources endogènes au service des villes religieuses. Le waqf n’est pas seulement un instrument financier, c’est une vision de solidarité et de pérennité au service des communautés. » Pour sa part, Dr Ahmed Lamine Athie, Directeur général de la Haute Autorité du Waqf, a souligné : « Notre ambition est de faire du waqf un levier structurant du développement territorial. Ce partenariat avec le PNAMVR traduit notre volonté commune d’articuler spiritualité, modernité et autonomie financière.»

items.title: Opération Phoenix : le Maroc participe à une vaste campagne d’Interpol contre le terrorisme
items.description: Les autorités sécuritaires marocaines ont pris part, aux côtés de leurs homologues d’Algérie, de Jordanie, de Palestine et de Tunisie, à une opération coordonnée par l’Organisation internationale de police criminelle (Interpol) visant à renforcer la lutte contre le terrorisme et la criminalité transfrontalière dans la région du Moyen-Orient et de l’Afrique du Nord. Baptisée « Opération Phoenix » , cette intervention de trois semaines a conduit à l’arrestation de 48 personnes, dont neuf faisant l’objet de recherches internationales : huit étaient visées par des notices rouges d’Interpol et une autre par une notice diffusée par l’organisation. L’opération a également permis de procéder à plusieurs saisies et de réaliser un important travail de vérification dans les bases de données policières internationales. Dans un communiqué, Interpol souligne que cette opération constitue une première dans la région par son mode de conduite : des policières ont assuré l’entière responsabilité opérationnelle de la mission, depuis les contrôles initiaux effectués aux points de passage jusqu’à la coordination des opérations aux frontières. Plus de 700.000 vérifications dans les bases d’Interpol Pendant les trois semaines de l’opération, les forces participantes ont effectué plus de 700.000 vérifications croisées avec les bases de données d’Interpol. Ces contrôles ont permis d’identifier 246 correspondances positives concernant des personnes ou des documents de voyage. L’opération a notamment permis de mettre la main sur cinq documents de voyage signalés dans la base d’Interpol consacrée aux documents volés et perdus. Les contrôles ont également conduit à la saisie de 11 véhicules de luxe, de 1,8 kilogramme d’or, de 13.000 comprimés de Captagon, de 123 capsules de méthamphétamine et de 1.525 paquets de cigarettes de contrebande. Les forces engagées ont également récupéré 530 téléphones portables, ainsi que des sommes d’argent estimées à plus de 16.000 dollars et 9.900 euros. © Interpol Ces résultats illustrent l’importance des contrôles aux frontières dans l’identification de personnes recherchées et la détection de documents ou de biens signalés dans les bases internationales. Pour Interpol, l’échange rapide d’informations entre les services nationaux constitue un élément central dans la lutte contre les réseaux criminels et les personnes recherchées au-delà de leurs pays d’origine. Deux fugitifs recherchés par la France arrêtés en Algérie Parmi les opérations citées par Interpol figurent deux arrestations particulièrement liées à des recherches judiciaires françaises. La première concerne un homme recherché dans le cadre d’une affaire de fusillade survenue à Toulouse en 2022. Il a été interpellé à l’aéroport international Houari-Boumédiène d’Alger. Selon Interpol, l’intéressé s’était auparavant évadé d’une prison après avoir été condamné à huit ans de réclusion pour des faits liés au trafic de stupéfiants, à une association criminelle et à la détention d’armes. Dans un autre dossier, un second fugitif recherché par les autorités françaises a été arrêté à un poste-frontière terrestre entre l’Algérie et la Tunisie. Il avait été condamné à 15 ans de prison pour meurtre avant de s’évader. Ces deux arrestations illustrent le rôle des contrôles transfrontaliers et des bases de données internationales dans la localisation de personnes susceptibles de circuler entre plusieurs pays de la région. © Interpol Des policières aux commandes de l’opération L’une des particularités de « Phoenix » réside dans la place accordée aux femmes policières. Interpol indique qu’il s’agit de la première opération menée dans la région MENA dans laquelle des policières ont assumé l’intégralité de la responsabilité opérationnelle. Leur intervention a couvert l’ensemble de la chaîne opérationnelle. Elles ont participé aux premières vérifications des documents et aux entretiens réalisés aux points de passage, avant d’assurer la conduite des opérations de contrôle aux frontières. Les policières ont également pris en charge la coopération internationale au sein des bureaux nationaux d’Interpol des cinq pays participants. Elles ont, en outre, coordonné les activités menées depuis les deux unités de coordination opérationnelle installées en Algérie et en Jordanie. Pour Interpol, cette expérience constitue un volet important de son travail visant à renforcer la participation des femmes aux opérations de maintien de l’ordre et aux dispositifs de coopération policière internationale. L’opération « Phoenix » s’inscrit à ce titre dans le cadre du projet Momentum-MENA, une initiative d’Interpol prévue sur trois ans pour renforcer les capacités nationales et régionales des services chargés de l’application de la loi dans la région du Moyen-Orient et de l’Afrique du Nord. Le programme accorde une attention particulière à la formation opérationnelle et au déploiement de policières dans les différentes structures concernées. Le Maroc au sein d’un dispositif régional La participation du Maroc à cette opération intervient dans un cadre régional associant plusieurs services de sécurité et de contrôle aux frontières. Le principe même de « Phoenix » repose sur le croisement des informations disponibles dans les bases d’Interpol avec les contrôles effectués sur le terrain. L’objectif est notamment de pouvoir identifier rapidement une personne recherchée, vérifier l’authenticité et le statut d’un document de voyage ou détecter un bien signalé, indépendamment du pays dans lequel le contrôle intervient. Selon Maria Carmen Muñoz González, directrice de la lutte contre le terrorisme à Interpol, l’arrestation de neuf personnes recherchées au niveau international, dont certaines déjà condamnées, démontre l’efficacité que peut produire la coopération policière internationale dans les points de passage considérés comme sensibles. La responsable d’Interpol a également salué le travail des policières qui ont assuré la responsabilité opérationnelle de l’ensemble de la mission. Avec « Phoenix », Interpol met ainsi en avant un double objectif : renforcer la circulation et l'exploitation des informations policières entre les pays de la région, tout en développant la présence des femmes dans les opérations de terrain et les structures de coopération internationale. Pour les cinq pays participants, dont le Maroc, l’opération aura surtout permis de confronter les informations issues des bases internationales aux contrôles réalisés sur le terrain, avec à la clé plusieurs dizaines d’arrestations et un volume important de saisies. The post Opération Phoenix : le Maroc participe à une vaste campagne d’Interpol contre le terrorisme appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Électricité, eau, accès aux soins : à Thide Nganadou, le plaidoyer des populations pour sortir de l’enclavement
items.description: Dans ce village de la commune de Sam Yabale, dans l’arrondissement de Darou Mouhty, département de Kébémer, les populations vivent avec plusieurs difficultés qui pèsent sur leur quotidien. L’absence d’électricité, l’enclavement, les problèmes d’accès à l’eau potable et les insuffisances dans la prise en charge sanitaire figurent parmi leurs principales préoccupations. Face à cette situation, elles lancent un plaidoyer en direction des pouvoirs publics. LOUGA- Niché dans les profondeurs du département de Kébémer, Thidé Nganadou semble comme posé au milieu d’une vaste étendue de verdure. Le village, rattaché à la commune de Sam Yabale, dans l’arrondissement de Darou Mouhty, reste cependant difficile d’accès en raison de son enclavement. Depuis la capitale régionale, il faut emprunter la route nationale en direction de Dahra Djolof. Après une trentaine de kilomètres, l’itinéraire conduit jusqu’à Thiamène. C’est là qu’il faut quitter l’axe principal et s’engager sur une piste rurale longue d’une quinzaine de kilomètres. En cette période d’hivernage, le décor change. De part et d’autre de la piste, un tapis herbacé recouvre le sol et donne à la campagne des allures de vaste prairie. Des troupeaux apparaissent au loin, occupés à brouter paisiblement sous la surveillance des bergers. Certains ont trouvé refuge à l’ombre des arbres, loin de la chaleur. Après environ une heure de trajet, Thidé Nganadou se dévoile enfin. À l’entrée du village, les habitations en dur côtoient encore les maisons traditionnelles. Une image qui témoigne du caractère rural de cette localité créée, selon les habitants, vers les années 1800. L’absence d’électricité figure parmi les principales doléances Majoritairement peuplé de Peuls, Thidé Nganadou vit essentiellement de l’agriculture et de l’élevage. La population est estimée à plus de 3 000 habitants. Mais derrière cette activité rurale, les habitants sont confrontés à des difficultés qui affectent plusieurs aspects de leur vie quotidienne. « Nous sommes dans des conditions très précaires, car nous manquons presque de tout », dénonce El Hadji Ka. Pour lui, le déficit d’électrification constitue un frein au développement de la localité. « Nous n’avons pas d’électricité. Cette absence de courant bloque le développement de notre communauté dans tous les domaines », déplore-t-il. Dans le village, cette situation touche également les enfants. « Nos enfants révisent leurs leçons à la lueur des bougies ou des lampes de poche », raconte le natif de Thidé Nganadou. Une situation qui, selon lui, rend les conditions d’apprentissage encore plus difficiles. Une piste qui complique les déplacements À l’absence d’électricité s’ajoute l’enclavement. Pour les populations, l’état des voies d’accès constitue un autre obstacle au développement du village. Djoumo Ka, représentant du chef de village, insiste sur cette difficulté. « En plus d’être enclavés, nous n’avons pas de route digne de ce nom », regrette-t-il. Il plaide pour le bitumage de l’axe Thiamène-Sam Yabale. Une infrastructure qui, selon lui, faciliterait les déplacements des populations, mais aussi l’évacuation et la commercialisation des productions agricoles et pastorales. L’eau potable, une autre préoccupation L’accès à une eau de qualité reste également au centre des préoccupations. Le village dispose bien d’un forage, mais la qualité de l’eau constitue un problème pour les habitants. Selon Isma Ba, l’eau est fortement salée. Une situation qui pose particulièrement problème aux femmes enceintes. « Nos femmes enceintes ne boivent pas cette eau », explique-t-il. Cette contrainte oblige ainsi les populations à chercher d’autres solutions pour disposer d’une eau jugée plus adaptée à la consommation. Le manque de sage-femme, une difficulté pour les femmes Dans le domaine de la santé, les populations soulignent également les limites du dispositif existant. Le poste de santé du village ne dispose pas de sage-femme, selon Djoumo Ka. Cette absence complique la prise en charge des femmes enceintes, particulièrement lorsque surviennent des situations nécessitant une intervention rapide. Pour les habitants, le renforcement du personnel de santé apparaît donc comme une nécessité pour améliorer la prise en charge sanitaire dans cette localité éloignée. Thidé Nganadou accueille également chaque année un gamou qui attire de nombreux fidèles venus de différentes localités. Ce rendez-vous religieux constitue un moment important pour la communauté. Les populations souhaitent toutefois un accompagnement plus conséquent des autorités lors de cet événement. Elles estiment que le soutien institutionnel reste insuffisant au regard de l’importance de la manifestation. Un plaidoyer pour sortir de l’isolement Électricité, route, eau potable, santé : les préoccupations exprimées par les habitants de Thidé Nganadou touchent ainsi à plusieurs secteurs essentiels de la vie quotidienne. À travers leurs témoignages, les populations lancent un appel aux autorités de l’État. Elles souhaitent voir leurs conditions de vie améliorées et leur village davantage intégré aux politiques publiques de développement. Pour ces habitants, le désenclavement, l’accès à l’électricité et à une eau de qualité, ainsi que le renforcement de l’offre sanitaire constituent autant de priorités pour permettre à Thidé Nganadou de mieux valoriser ses activités agricoles et pastorales et d’offrir de meilleures conditions de vie à ses populations. Falel PAM (correspondant)

items.title: Burkina: création d’une Inspection générale des ressources humaines
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 17 septembre 2026). ‎Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a présidé ce jeudi, l’hebdomadaire Conseil des ministres. Selon le Ministre Porte-parole du Gouvernement, Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert OUÉDRAOGO, le Conseil a examiné d’importants dossiers et pris des décisions pour répondre aux aspirations profondes du Peuple burkinabè conformément aux orientations de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire (RPP). Au titre du ministère des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Conseil a adopté un décret portant création et organisation de l'Inspection générale des ressources humaines. Pour le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple, le Camarade Mathias TRAORÉ « la création de l'Inspection générale des ressources humaines s'inscrit dans la dynamique de la transformation profonde de l’administration et conformément aux exigences de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire ». Pour le Ministre TRAORÉ, la Commission de régulation des dysfonctionnements (CRD) a procédé à un diagnostic de l'ensemble des dysfonctionnements de l'Administration publique au cours de l'année 2025. « Il s'est trouvé que les dysfonctionnements qui ont été relevés ne seront pas entièrement couverts par les conseils de discipline qui sont mis en place. Il se trouve aussi que le personnel de l'État constitue des ressources qui sont mises à la disposition des autres administrations », soutient le Ministre des Serviteurs du Peuple. C’est pourquoi, selon lui, le gouvernement a décidé de la création d’une structure transversale à mesure d'auditer et de contrôler la gestion qui est faite de l'ensemble de ses ressources humaines, y compris celles mises à la disposition des institutions et autres structures publiques. L’Inspection générale des ressources humaines permettra « d'avoir avec précision l'effectif des agents dans l'Administration publique, de contrôler l'utilisation qui est faite de ce personnel et enfin de voir la rémunération qui en découle afin de maîtriser les effectifs et la masse salariale », a soutenu le Ministre. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso L’article Burkina: création d'une Inspection générale des ressources humaines est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: ‘The Best Thing That Happened to Him Was Losing in 2020’
items.description: Few reporters understand as much about Donald Trump’s thinking, motives, and behavior as Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan. Haberman has been covering the president closely for more than a decade at The New York Times ; she started with his first campaign in 2015, and her record of scoops quickly brought her into the public eye. Swan was, for many years, her chief professional rival: He worked for Axios , where he landed a controversial 2018 one-on-one interview with Trump . In late 2022, the Times announced that it was hiring Swan, turning the rivals into colleagues. This past June, they published Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump . The book, an instant best seller, advances a new understanding of the first year of Trump’s second term, relaying in minute-by-minute detail how, since retaking office, he has pursued his personal goals with few limits on his power. The Atlantic staff writer Tim Alberta sat down with both authors at The Atlantic Festival, where he asked them about the 2028 election and the future of the presidency and the Republican Party. This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity. Tim Alberta: Maggie, this country has been through a lot, and I’m wondering if you could help us understand how a “regime change” of this sort came to be. Maggie Haberman: Essentially, we have had a series of national traumas since 9/11: two forever wars, a fiscal crisis, immense populist anger that started rising in 2010. To me, that was the year that set the tone. It was also the year that the proto-Trump, Carl Paladino, was the Republican nominee for governor in New York State. One of the issues that he ran on was the planned mosque to be built near the World Trade Center; it became known incorrectly as the “Ground Zero Mosque,” and it became a clear avatar of a change in this country after the era of George W. Bush. So you get to 2014, when immigration and particularly border crossings were on the rise under President Obama. Suddenly, this became a massive issue within the Republican Party. You had this mix of anger over the wars, anger over the massive accumulated debt under President Bush, then Obamacare, anger about immigration, and a shifting job market. The time was ripe for a candidate who presented himself as a fighter—and who was already known to most of the Republican electorate, not just as a celebrity on The Apprentice but as a cultural figure. Alberta: 2016, Trump 1.0, is its own story. So much of what this book is about is how the end of that first term, and then his time in exile after losing in 2020, shapes this dramatic, radical, wholesale change to government and to executive power. Jonathan Swan: When we were reporting for this book, we heard from a couple of people who were close to Trump at a pretty high level that, in their view, the best thing that happened to him was losing in 2020. Which is something they could never say publicly or in his presence, because, of course, he never lost the election and what have you. But it’s indisputably true. Let’s say Trump ekes out that victory in 2020: He comes back in; he is hobbled by COVID. He has the same inflation that every other country around the world has. He still has the rump of a team around him that he really doesn’t like very much, who are, in quite a few instances, pushing back on some of his more extreme desires. He really can’t get his arms around the presidency. Instead, he loses. People like Stephen Miller spent those four years very productively. It wasn’t just drawing up the plans—you saw that blitz of executive orders at the start of 2025, which was all very well prepared. They also spent a lot of time thinking about Who are the lawyers that we want to fill the government with? And I’m not just talking about the White House counsel’s office; I’m talking about across the government. Agency lawyers, general counsels—they would constantly say, Well, no, what you’re proposing is illegal . But when you have lawyers who are saying, Well, actually, if we turn it this way and then turn it this way and then give it a little bit of a spin , then they can bless what you want. And that’s what’s happening. I’ll give you the perfect example that describes the difference between term one and term two: In term one, Trump was saying almost yearningly, You know, they don’t have a drug problem in China, because Xi Jinping, he just kills the drug dealers. And they don’t have a drug problem in the Philippines, because Rodrigo Duterte just kills them . Trump was very fond of these extrajudicial killings. In term one, there wasn’t a huge amount of enthusiasm for this idea among the leadership of the Defense Department. Now you have Pete Hegseth, and you have lawyers inside the government that allow a policy where Donald Trump decided, in his mind, that people on fishing boats transporting cocaine in the Caribbean Sea are not drug traffickers who are to be interdicted by the Coast Guard and dealt with in a criminal-justice system. No: They’re enemy combatants in a war. We’re not going to interdict them. We’re not going to arrest them. We’re just going to kill them . And that’s something that has been blessed within the government. They haven’t even bothered to try to legally justify this in a public setting. They just do it, knowing that they have the right lawyers in place. [ Read: Pete Hegseth delights in violence ] The other big element making this term unrecognizable from the first term is the immunity decision. Maggie and I talk about this all the time. Trump would say early on, I’m immune; I’m immune . He has said privately that he’s going to pardon anyone who came within 250 feet of the Oval Office. The point is, he had the time to rebuild, and his team had time to prepare. That’s how you get this second term. Alberta: Trump can’t stay in power forever. He will soon be a lame duck after these November midterms. I’m wondering how he’s handling that: whether he is going to allow a neat and tidy process to unfold for his successor, and whether or not J. D. Vance, who got a bit crosswise with him over Iran, is going to be tortured over the next several years as the president deliberates over whom he should hand all of this over to. Swan: We have a scene in the book that I think illustrates what you’re describing. Rupert Murdoch comes to the White House for dinner. This is October of last year, and they’re in the Blue Room of the White House. And at the table are J. D. Vance and Marco Rubio. Haberman: And, like, 10 other people. Swan: Halfway through the conversation, Trump says, I really like J.D. I really like Marco. Rupert, what do you think of J.D.? And he starts this beauty pageant, essentially, in front of both of them, with the most powerful proprietor of conservative media—knowing full well that Rupert Murdoch is no fan of J. D. Vance and, in fact, tried to stop him from becoming the vice president. There’s this pause, and Rupert Murdoch says, J.D. has the potential to be great —just withering. Vance says, Oh, gee, thanks, Rupert . It’s a very awkward moment. Trump says, What do you think of Marco? And Rupert doesn’t miss a beat: He says, Marco’s brilliant . This savage moment just foretells what the next two years are going to be like. How is he grappling with being a lame duck? The way he’s grappling with it is by refusing to be a lame duck. [ Read: Vance vs. Rubio: Iran edition ] Vance is in a really difficult position because, as you noted, there were several meetings leading up to the Iran war, in the Situation Room and the Oval Office, where Vance was the only one in the room arguing against it. That did not go down well with Trump. And so the notion that this is going to be some smooth glide path to the 2028 nomination is contradicted by every piece of evidence we have about who Donald Trump is and how he behaves. Alberta: Maggie, that point that Jonathan makes about Trump’s refusal to be a lame duck over the next two years—what does that look like? Haberman: I don’t want to limit anyone’s imagination here on what it would look like. The question that we get a lot is, Will he try for a third term? I truly don’t believe he will, but I’m absolutely willing to be wrong. I don’t actually think he wants that, and he doesn’t need it. He will be the dominant figure in this party until he is no longer on this Earth, whether he’s in office or not. He has made more money than he ever made in his life during this presidency—at least just liquid, that we know of, assets. Swan: By orders of magnitude. Haberman: The crypto money is, I think, $2.2 billion in the first year-ish of the presidency. His children have continued to make money. There were very valid questions about Hunter Biden, but it is so dwarfed by everything that we are seeing now, everything that Hunter Biden was doing. What the next two years I expect will look like will be the projects Trump really cares about , which are these monuments to himself in Washington—the ballroom. I’m very curious to see what happens with the Kennedy Center ; that’s a big open question. This is not going to look like any kind of congressional flip that we’ve seen before in a lame-duck presidency, because to Jonathan’s point, Trump knows that he is immune from federal prosecution. He has talked about pardons very openly. We spoke with a number of people who are counting on their pardons. We’ve never seen a government just not respond to subpoenas in Congress. The only recourse that Congress has if they don’t get cooperation is a contempt-of-Congress vote and a referral to the Department of Justice, where I’m confident Attorney General Todd Blanche is not going to do a lot. This is a government that has done so little in terms of legislating. Everything, for the most part, was by executive action. Alberta: Your reporting describes a government that is not recognizable at a fundamental level. How do we come back from that? Haberman: That’s the reason for the title. Swan: It’s such an interesting question, because on the one hand, there will be a desire by many to restore what was before. On the other hand, Trump has also shown what you can do unilaterally. He’s demonstrated, particularly in the second term, that a lot of the constraints that we take for granted around the presidency are not legal constraints. They’re self-restraint or norms. Just take the ballroom, for example. Yes, in the end, it was green-lighted, right? The court system is not stopping him from building this ballroom. But by the time the court system got up to that point, there was a giant hole in the ground. There were cranes in the sky; there were shovels going through the earth. [ Leah Litman: The court’s ballroom decision is a sign of deeper problems ] The tariffs are another great example: Yes, ultimately, the Supreme Court checked him on his tariffs—months after he started a global trade war, which had all kinds of rippling consequences. This is a legal system that is not built to deal with a president like Donald Trump; he has shown that you can just get away with acting and forcing others to react. That was a deliberate strategy—overwhelm the opposition; overwhelm the legal groups. So you have two models: One is a figure who comes back and says, Actually, we need to restore checks and balances and the constitutional system . Or you have either a right-wing populist or a left-wing populist saying, You know what? Donald Trump has actually shown us what nirvana could look like if we do it on behalf of our chosen priorities . That’s how you can get potentially even more of an expansion of executive power and the imperial presidency. Haberman: The one addendum I would make is that I think that for the most part, President Biden did try going back. He really did. He did fairly little by executive action; he had big legislation; he left the Justice Department alone. What I hear from Democrats I speak with is that they want someone who is going to fight in the manner that they have seen Republicans fight. I agree with Jonathan that I don’t think there is another Donald Trump walking around; I think he is sui generis for a lot of reasons. But that doesn’t mean there are not aspects that would be appealing. And certainly, I believe that whoever the next Republican nominee is, they’re going to be in the mold of Donald Trump. I mean, this is Donald Trump’s party until there is another Republican president, not just nominee, or for as long as he is alive. Whatever you see the Democrats form will be a reaction to that. The only other asterisk is that if ever there was an election cycle that was ripe for a Ross Perot type, it will be 2028. There is so much anger at the system. Part of why Trump is struggling right now in polls is that he broke several campaign promises, and voters can feel that. They can feel $4.50 gas. People want to feel like somebody is actually helping them. When you buy a book using a link on this page, we receive a commission. Thank you for supporting The Atlantic .

items.title: Nasser Bourita s'entretient avec António Guterres au siège de l'ONU
items.description: Le ministre des Affaires étrangères, de la Coopération africaine et des Marocains résidant à l’étranger, Nasser Bourita, s’est entretenu avec le Secrétaire général des Nations Unies, António Guterres, mercredi au siège de l’ONU à New York. Durant cette réunion, le Secrétaire général de l’ONU a chargé le ministre de transmettre au Roi Mohammed VI, ses salutations fraternelles et respectueuses, ainsi que son admiration pour l’engagement du Royaume du Maroc en faveur du multilatéralisme et pour ses positions courageuses en défense des trois piliers des Nations Unies, même dans des situations complexes. Notant que le monde traverse des moments difficiles, avec des crises qui s’aggravent et des guerres qui s’élargissent, M. Guterres a tempéré en constatant que le Maroc, si heureusement, se porte bien grâce au Leadership du Roi. A cet égard, il a exprimé son admiration pour le rôle joué par la diplomatie marocaine, agissante, élégante et déterminée, sous la conduite du Souverain, tant au sein des Nations Unies que sur la scène internationale. A cette occasion, M. Bourita a transmis les salutations amicales du Roi Mohammed VI, ainsi que Sa haute appréciation pour la coopération qui a marqué les relations entre le Maroc et les Nations Unis durant les deux mandats du Secrétaire général de l’ONU, depuis 2016. The post Nasser Bourita s'entretient avec António Guterres au siège de l'ONU appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Haho : Des kits scolaires aux meilleurs élèves aux différents examens
items.description: Notsè, 17 sept. (ATOP) – Les meilleurs élèves aux différents examens nationaux ont bénéficié, le mercredi 16 septembre à Notsè, des kits scolaires offerts par la mairie Haho 1. Composé de sacs, cahiers, écritoires, ensemble-géométrie, règles, le geste est à la fois un soutien et une motivation à l’endroit des meilleurs apprenants de la commune Haho 1. Il vise à les soutenir pour une bonne rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 afin de créer l’émulation pour un meilleur rendement. Remise symbolique par le Maire Les bénéficiaires, en recevant les kits ont été encouragés à persévérer dans l’excellence et le respect des biens publics qui sont la devise de la commune Haho 1. Ils ont été aussi conviés à être des modèles pour inciter les autres élèves à de meilleurs rendements scolaires. Pour le maire de la commune Haho 1, Koffi Assila, ce geste financé sur les fonds propres de la commune permet de soutenir les meilleurs aux différents examens (CEPD, BEPC, BAC 1et BAC 2) et de promouvoir la culture de l’excellence. Il a demandé aux bénéficiaires de maintenir l’élan et l’ardeur au travail, afin de hisser la commune au rang des meilleures au Togo. « L’éclosion de la commune Haho 1 doit s’appuyer sur les efforts consentis par ses fils et filles », a-t-il précisé. Le chef de l’Inspection de l’enseignement primaire et préscolaire (IEPP-Haho) Sud, Alossé Kossi a invité les parents et tuteurs à encadrer les apprenants pour de meilleurs résultats. ATOP/YM/AR

items.title: Bauxite, rail, port en eau profonde : ce méga-projet chinois de 3 milliards de dollars qui se dessine en Guinée
items.description: Le Premier ministre Amadou Oury Bah a reçu, ce jeudi 16 septembre 2026, une délégation d’un consortium d’entreprises chinoises venue lui présenter le projet du Grand corridor de Guinée, une importante infrastructure minière et logistique destinée à relier les zones minières de Santou à un futur port en eau profonde à Cape Verga. Piloté notamment par SPIC et Chinalco, le consortium envisage la construction d’une ligne ferroviaire d’environ 160 kilomètres reliant Santou à Cape Verga. Le projet prévoit également l’aménagement d’un port en eau profonde capable d’accueillir des navires d’une capacité allant jusqu’à 200 000 tonnes. Selon les éléments présentés au cours de la rencontre, l’investissement global nécessaire à la réalisation de ce projet est estimé à plus de 3 milliards de dollars américains. Une capacité d’évacuation de 77 millions de tonnes de bauxite Le Grand corridor devrait permettre d’évacuer environ 77 millions de tonnes de bauxite par an, grâce à la mise en place de cette nouvelle chaîne ferroviaire et portuaire. À travers cette infrastructure, les promoteurs ambitionnent de créer une liaison directe entre les zones d’exploitation minières et la façade maritime, tout en renforçant les capacités logistiques nécessaires à l’acheminement de la production. Un nouveau corridor minier et logistique La présentation de ce projet intervient dans un contexte marqué par l’accélération du développement des infrastructures minières, ferroviaires et portuaires en Guinée. Les échanges entre le chef du gouvernement et les représentants du consortium ont notamment porté sur les différentes composantes du Grand corridor, les modalités de sa réalisation ainsi que ses perspectives de développement. À travers ce projet, les partenaires chinois entendent contribuer à la mise en place d’un nouvel axe stratégique pour l’évacuation de la bauxite guinéenne et au renforcement des infrastructures de transport et de logistique du pays.
